\begin{abstract}
Let $M$ be a set acted on by a group $G$ of symmetries, and let an \emph{external interpretation} be an arbitrary map $I : M \to V$ into a value set $V$ regarded as lying outside the structure. We ask when such an interpretation is \emph{recoverable from structural truth}, i.e.\ when it factors through the quotient of $M$ by structural indistinguishability, and when it is moreover \emph{definable} in a language of invariant predicates.

We prove that recoverability is exactly orbit constancy, with a unique factorisation, and that the orbit map is the universal recoverable interpretation. In any invariant language, definability implies orbit constancy, so the conjunction ``orbit-constant and definable'' is redundant. For the \emph{maximal} invariant language --- the algebra of all invariant sets --- definability and recoverability coincide with no cardinality hypotheses. For bounded invariant languages on infinite carriers the two notions come apart: parity on $\mathbb{N}$ with trivial symmetry group is recoverable but undefinable in the finite/cofinite language. For finite carriers we prove a four-way collapse: recoverable $\iff$ orbit-constant $\iff$ definable in the maximal invariant language $\iff$ each fibre is a Boolean combination of orbit-counting predicates; and the counting enrichment is necessary, since the trivial invariant language defines no non-constant interpretation.

Quantitatively we introduce the \emph{meaning-loss exponent} $\ell(M) = |M| - \#\Orb(M)$ and prove: the interpretation count factors as $|V|^{|M|} = |V|^{\#\Orb}\cdot|V|^{\ell(M)}$; $\ell$ is additive over disjoint unions; $\ell(M) = 0$ exactly for rigid models, equivalently exactly when every interpretation is recoverable; and $\ell(M) = \sum_O(|O|-1)$. Combining with the orbit-counting lemma yields $2^{\sum_g |\Fix(g)|} = R^{|G|}$, where $R$ is the number of recoverable Boolean interpretations. A logical-invariance theorem shows that over a structureless carrier of arbitrary cardinality an interpretation of finitely many coordinates is recoverable iff it depends only on the kernel of the tuple --- only equality is logical --- with finiteness of arity shown to be sharp. Finally, a Krasner-style reconstruction theorem shows a permutation lies in $G$ iff it preserves every $G$-recoverable interpretation of configurations, so $G \mapsto \Th(G)$ is injective and strictly antitone.
\end{abstract}

\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} external interpretation, orbit descent, invariant language, definability, permutation invariance, meaning-loss exponent, Burnside's lemma, Galois connection.

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

A structure sees its own elements only up to its symmetries. When we lay an external labelling on top of a structure --- colours on vertices, names on database entries, gauge choices on a field configuration, coordinates on a manifold --- some of what we write down is intrinsic to the object and some is ours. The purpose of this paper is to make that distinction exact, to determine which languages can express the intrinsic part, and to measure the discarded part with a numerical invariant.

The setting is deliberately minimal. Let $G$ be a group acting on a set $M$. We think of $G$ as the automorphism group of whatever structure $M$ carries; the framework is indifferent to what that structure is, since only the induced action matters. An \emph{external interpretation} is any function $I : M \to V$ into an arbitrary value set $V$.

Two elements $x,y \in M$ are \emph{structurally indistinguishable}, written $x \sim_G y$, when $g\cdot x = y$ for some $g \in G$. This is an equivalence relation and coincides with the orbit relation. Write $M/G$ for the orbit space, $\pi : M \to M/G$ for the quotient map and $[x]$ for the class of $x$.

We say $I$ is \emph{recoverable from structural truth} when there exists $F : M/G \to V$ with $F \circ \pi = I$, and \emph{orbit-constant} when $x \sim_G y$ implies $I(x) = I(y)$.

\subsection{The conjecture under test}

The investigation was organised around the following conjecture: an external interpretation is recoverable exactly when it is constant on automorphism orbits \emph{and} definable in the invariant language; for finite models, orbit constancy alone suffices after adding bounded counting modalities.

Our results show the conjecture is neither simply true nor simply false: it is \emph{under-specified}, and the three regimes it conflates have three different answers.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item The conjunction is \textbf{redundant}: definability in any invariant language already entails orbit constancy (Theorem~\ref{thm:defoc}).
\item With ``the invariant language'' read as the \emph{maximal} one, the conjecture is \textbf{true}, with no finiteness (Theorem~\ref{thm:maxlang}).
\item With a \emph{bounded} invariant language, the conjecture is \textbf{false} on infinite carriers (Theorem~\ref{thm:parity}).
\item The finite half is \textbf{true} and the counting enrichment is \textbf{necessary} (Theorems~\ref{thm:finiteclass} and \ref{thm:countstronger}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Preliminaries}

Throughout, $G$ is a group acting on a set $M$, and $V,W$ are value sets. No finiteness is assumed unless stated.

\begin{definition}[Structural indistinguishability]
For $x,y \in M$ write $x \sim_G y$ iff $\exists g \in G,\ g\cdot x = y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
$\sim_G$ is an equivalence relation, and $x \sim_G y$ iff $x \in \Orb_G(y)$ iff $y \in \Orb_G(x)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Reflexivity from $1\cdot x = x$; symmetry from $g^{-1}\cdot(g\cdot x) = x$; transitivity from $(hg)\cdot x = h\cdot(g\cdot x)$. The identification with orbit membership is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Invariant set]
$S \subseteq M$ is \emph{invariant} if $x \in S \Rightarrow g\cdot x \in S$ for all $g \in G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:closure}
$\emptyset$ is invariant; each orbit $\Orb_G(x)$ is invariant; invariant sets are closed under complement, union, intersection and difference.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For orbits: if $y = g'\cdot x$ then $g\cdot y = (gg')\cdot x$. For complements: if $S$ is invariant and $x \notin S$ but $g\cdot x \in S$, then $x = g^{-1}\cdot(g\cdot x) \in S$, a contradiction. For unions: case split. Intersection and difference follow by De Morgan.
\end{proof}

\section{Orbit descent}

\begin{theorem}[Orbit descent]\label{thm:descent}
$I : M \to V$ is recoverable from structural truth if and only if it is orbit-constant.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) If $F\circ\pi = I$ and $x \sim_G y$ then $\pi(x) = \pi(y)$, so $I(x) = F(\pi(x)) = F(\pi(y)) = I(y)$.

($\Leftarrow$) If $I$ is orbit-constant it is constant on the fibres of $\pi$, hence descends to $F([x]) := I(x)$, well defined by the universal property of quotients, and $F\circ\pi = I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of recovery]\label{thm:unique}
If $F_1\circ\pi = I$ and $F_2\circ\pi = I$ then $F_1 = F_2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\pi$ is surjective and $F_1([x]) = I(x) = F_2([x])$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Meaning collision]
If $x \sim_G y$ and $I(x) \neq I(y)$ then $I$ is not recoverable.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Total annihilation under full symmetry]\label{thm:annih}
Let $G = \Sym(M)$ act naturally. Then $I$ is recoverable iff $I$ is constant.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For $x \neq y$ the transposition $(x\ y)$ carries $x$ to $y$, so all elements are indistinguishable and orbit constancy is global constancy; the converse is trivial. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}
On $M = \{\tp,\fp\}$ under $\Sym(M)$, the identity interpretation is not recoverable: it is the smallest meaning collision.
\end{example}

\begin{theorem}[Universality of the orbit map]
$\pi$ is recoverable, and every recoverable $I : M \to V$ factors through $\pi$ by a unique $F$. Hence $\pi$ is the finest recoverable interpretation of $M$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\pi$ is recoverable via $F = \mathrm{id}$; existence is Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} and uniqueness Theorem~\ref{thm:unique}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Closure properties]\label{prop:closure}
If $I : M \to V$ and $J : M \to W$ are recoverable and $\varphi : V \to V'$ is any function, then $\varphi\circ I$ and $x \mapsto (I(x),J(x))$ are recoverable; conversely every $\varphi\circ\pi$ is recoverable.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Immediate from orbit constancy, componentwise.
\end{proof}

Proposition~\ref{prop:closure} says the recoverable interpretations of $M$ form the clone generated by the orbit map: the orbit map is not just \emph{an} invariant but \emph{the} invariant, and all others are its renamings.

\section{Invariant languages and definability}

\begin{definition}[Invariant language]
An \emph{invariant language} on $(G,M)$ is a family $\mathcal{L}$ of subsets of $M$ with $\emptyset \in \mathcal{L}$, closed under complement and union, all of whose members are invariant.
\end{definition}

The first three clauses make $\mathcal{L}$ the algebra of extensions of a propositional language closed under $\bot,\neg,\vee$; the fourth is the semantic content: the language talks only about the structure.

\begin{definition}[Definability]
$I : M \to V$ is \emph{definable in} $\mathcal{L}$ when every fibre $I^{-1}(v)$ belongs to $\mathcal{L}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Definability entails orbit constancy]\label{thm:defoc}
If $I$ is definable in some invariant language $\mathcal{L}$ then $I$ is orbit-constant.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $y = g\cdot x$. The fibre $S = I^{-1}(I(x)) \in \mathcal{L}$ contains $x$, hence by invariance contains $g\cdot x = y$, i.e.\ $I(y) = I(x)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Redundancy]
For any invariant language $\mathcal{L}$, ``$I$ definable in $\mathcal{L}$'' is equivalent to ``$I$ orbit-constant and definable in $\mathcal{L}$''. The conjunction in the conjecture carries no information beyond its second conjunct.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:defrec}
Definability in any invariant language implies recoverability.
\end{corollary}

\section{The maximal language and the finite collapse}

\begin{definition}
The \emph{orbit language} $\mathcal{O}$ is the family of \emph{all} invariant subsets of $M$.
\end{definition}

By Lemma~\ref{lem:closure} it is an invariant language, and by the invariance clause every invariant language is contained in it: $\mathcal{O}$ is the maximal invariant language.

\begin{theorem}[Maximal-language theorem]\label{thm:maxlang}
For every $I : M \to V$, with no finiteness hypothesis, $I$ is definable in $\mathcal{O}$ if and only if $I$ is recoverable from structural truth.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) Corollary~\ref{cor:defrec}. ($\Leftarrow$) If $I$ is orbit-constant, $x \in I^{-1}(v)$ and $g \in G$, then $I(g\cdot x) = I(x) = v$, so every fibre is invariant.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:maxlang} is the correct general form of the conjecture: recoverability \emph{is} definability, in the largest invariant language. Finiteness serves only to replace that abstract language by a finitely generated one.

\begin{definition}
The \emph{counting language} $\mathcal{C}$ is the smallest family of subsets of $M$ containing every orbit and $\emptyset$ and closed under complement and union.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness and finite completeness]\label{thm:countgen}
Every member of $\mathcal{C}$ is invariant. Conversely, if $M$ is finite then every invariant subset of $M$ lies in $\mathcal{C}$. Hence $\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{O}$ for finite $M$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Soundness is induction on the generation of $\mathcal{C}$ using Lemma~\ref{lem:closure}.

Completeness is strong induction on $|S|$ for invariant $S$. If $S = \emptyset$, done. Otherwise pick $x \in S$; invariance gives $\Orb_G(x) \subseteq S$ and $x \in \Orb_G(x)$, so $S \setminus \Orb_G(x)$ is strictly smaller and invariant (Lemma~\ref{lem:closure}), hence in $\mathcal{C}$ by induction. Then $S = \Orb_G(x) \cup (S\setminus\Orb_G(x))$ exhibits $S$ as a union of two members of $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{proof}

The proof is an algorithm: peel orbits off one at a time. It terminates in at most $\#\Orb(M)$ rounds and returns an explicit orbit decomposition --- the normal form of an invariant predicate on a finite model.

\begin{theorem}[Finite classification]\label{thm:finiteclass}
Let $M$ be finite and $I : M \to V$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $I$ is recoverable from structural truth;
\item $I$ is constant on automorphism orbits;
\item $I$ is definable in the maximal invariant language $\mathcal{O}$;
\item every fibre $I^{-1}(v)$ is a Boolean combination of orbit predicates.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
(1)$\iff$(2) is Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}; (1)$\iff$(3) is Theorem~\ref{thm:maxlang}; (3)$\iff$(4) is Theorem~\ref{thm:countgen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}
The \emph{trivial invariant language} $\mathcal{T}$ consists of $\emptyset$ and $M$ only.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:trivblind}
No non-constant interpretation is definable in $\mathcal{T}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
If $I(x)\neq I(y)$ then $S = I^{-1}(I(x))$ contains $x$ and misses $y$, so $S \notin \{\emptyset,M\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Counting modalities strictly increase expressive power]\label{thm:countstronger}
Let $M$ be finite and suppose $x \not\sim_G y$. Then the orbit indicator $\chi_x$, equal to $\tp$ on $\Orb_G(x)$ and $\fp$ elsewhere, is recoverable and definable in $\mathcal{C}$, but not definable in $\mathcal{T}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\chi_x$ is invariant since orbits are, so its fibres lie in $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{C}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:countgen}, and it is recoverable by Theorem~\ref{thm:finiteclass}. But $\chi_x(x) = \tp \neq \fp = \chi_x(y)$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:trivblind} applies.
\end{proof}

\section{The infinite boundary}

\begin{definition}
Let $M = \mathbb{N}$ carry the action of the trivial group $G = \{1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:trivgroup}
Under the trivial group, $\sim_G$ is equality; hence every interpretation of $\mathbb{N}$ is orbit-constant and recoverable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $S$ finite or $S^c$ finite.
\end{definition}

$\mathcal{F}$ is an invariant language: it contains $\emptyset$, is closed under complement by symmetry of the definition, is closed under union (a union of two finite sets is finite; if either set is cofinite so is the union), and invariance is automatic. Intuitively, a formula of $\mathcal{F}$ can pin down only finitely much information, or its negation can.

\begin{theorem}[The definability boundary is real]\label{thm:parity}
Let $\parity(n) = [\,n \text{ even}\,]$. Then $\parity$ is orbit-constant, hence recoverable, but is not definable in $\mathcal{F}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Orbit constancy is Lemma~\ref{lem:trivgroup}. The fibre $\parity^{-1}(\tp)$ is the set of even numbers, infinite (it contains $2k$ for all $k$, and $k \mapsto 2k$ is injective), with infinite complement (it omits $2k+1$ for all $k$). So the fibre is neither finite nor cofinite.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
There is a recoverable but undefinable interpretation; the implication ``recoverable $\Rightarrow$ definable'' fails for bounded invariant languages on infinite carriers.
\end{corollary}

The reconciliation with Theorem~\ref{thm:maxlang} is instructive: with the trivial group every subset of $\mathbb{N}$ is invariant, so the maximal language is the full power set and contains the evens. What fails for $\mathcal{F}$ is not invariance but expressive capacity. On finite carriers no such gap can open, by Theorem~\ref{thm:countgen}. Infinity is exactly what allows an invariant language to be incomplete.

\section{Graphs: a worked laboratory}

\begin{definition}
For a simple graph $\Gamma$ on vertex set $W$, $\Aut(\Gamma) \le \Sym(W)$ is the subgroup of permutations $\sigma$ with $\Gamma(\sigma a,\sigma b) \iff \Gamma(a,b)$ for all $a,b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Degree is recoverable]
For a finite graph $\Gamma$, the vertex-degree interpretation $v \mapsto \deg_\Gamma(v)$ is recoverable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
An automorphism $\sigma$ maps the neighbourhood of $v$ bijectively onto that of $\sigma v$, so $\deg(\sigma v)=\deg(v)$: degree is orbit-constant. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete graphs annihilate meaning]
Every permutation of $W$ is an automorphism of the complete graph $K_W$; consequently an interpretation of $K_W$ is recoverable iff it is constant.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Adjacency in $K_W$ is $a\neq b$, preserved by every bijection; then Theorem~\ref{thm:annih}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete classification for the $3$-path]
Let $P_3$ be the path $0-1-2$. Then $\Aut(P_3) = \{\mathrm{id},(0\ 2)\}$, and an interpretation $I$ of $P_3$ is recoverable iff $I(0)=I(2)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The endpoint swap preserves the two edges, and any automorphism must fix the unique degree-$2$ vertex, leaving only the identity and that swap; exhausting the six permutations confirms it. Given the group, orbit constancy says exactly $I(0)=I(2)$, and conversely this single equation gives constancy on both orbits $\{0,2\}$ and $\{1\}$. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
Vertex labels on $P_3$ are not recoverable, while degrees are, with $\deg 0 = \deg 2 = 1 \neq 2 = \deg 1$; thus degree on $P_3$ is not merely recoverable but \emph{separating}, exactly as fine as structural truth permits.
\end{corollary}

\section{Quantitative theory: the meaning-loss exponent}

In this section $M$ and $V$ are finite, $n = |M|$ and $k = \#\Orb_G(M)$.

\begin{theorem}[Count of recoverable interpretations]\label{thm:count}
The recoverable interpretations $M \to V$ correspond bijectively to the functions $M/G \to V$; hence there are exactly $|V|^k$ of them.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Theorems~\ref{thm:descent} and \ref{thm:unique} the map $I \mapsto F$ and the map $F \mapsto F\circ\pi$ are mutually inverse. Counting functions on a $k$-element domain gives $|V|^k$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Meaning-loss exponent]
$\ell(M) := n - k = |M| - \#\Orb_G(M)$.
\end{definition}

Since $\pi$ is surjective, $k \le n$ and $\ell(M) \ge 0$.

\begin{theorem}[Meaning-loss factorisation]
$|V|^{n} = |V|^{k}\cdot|V|^{\ell(M)}$: the total interpretation count is the recoverable count times a pure loss factor.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:count} and $n = k + \ell(M)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strictness]
If $|V|\ge 2$ and some orbit is non-trivial, strictly fewer interpretations are recoverable than exist.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A non-trivial orbit makes $\pi$ non-injective; surjective and non-injective on finite sets forces $k<n$, whence $|V|^k < |V|^n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Burnside bridge]
Let $R$ be the number of recoverable interpretations $M \to \{\tp,\fp\}$. Then
\[
2^{\;\sum_{g \in G}|\Fix(g)|} \;=\; R^{\,|G|}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:count} with $|V|=2$ gives $R = 2^k$; the orbit-counting lemma gives $\sum_g |\Fix(g)| = k|G|$; hence $2^{k|G|} = (2^k)^{|G|}$.
\end{proof}

The identity converts a semantic quantity --- how many meanings a structure can hold --- into a group-theoretic character sum.

\begin{lemma}[Orbits of a disjoint union]\label{lem:sumorb}
$(M \sqcup N)/G \cong (M/G)\sqcup(N/G)$, hence $\#\Orb(M\sqcup N) = \#\Orb(M)+\#\Orb(N)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The action preserves the two summands, so sending the class of $\iota_M(a)$ to $\iota_{M/G}([a])$ and the class of $\iota_N(b)$ to $\iota_{N/G}([b])$ is well defined; the evident map back is well defined for the same reason, and the composites are the identity on representatives.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity]
$\ell(M \sqcup N) = \ell(M) + \ell(N)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$|M\sqcup N| = |M|+|N|$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:sumorb}, using $\#\Orb(M)\le|M|$ and $\#\Orb(N)\le|N|$.
\end{proof}

Additivity marks $\ell$ as an extensive invariant, like entropy or dimension.

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity criterion]
$\ell(M)=0$ if and only if $M$ is \emph{rigid}: $x \sim_G y \Rightarrow x = y$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\ell(M)=0$ means $|M| = |M/G|$; $\pi$ is surjective, so equality of finite cardinalities makes it bijective, in particular injective, i.e.\ rigid. Conversely rigidity makes $\pi$ injective, so $|M|\le|M/G|$ and hence $\ell(M)=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity as total recoverability]
Suppose $|V|\ge 2$. Then $\ell(M)=0$ iff every interpretation $M \to V$ is recoverable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $\ell(M)=0$ then indistinguishability is equality and orbit constancy is vacuous. Conversely, if every interpretation is recoverable but $x\sim_G y$ with $x\neq y$, pick $v_0\neq v_1$ in $V$ and set $I(z)=v_0$ if $z=x$, else $v_1$; recoverability forces $v_0 = I(x) = I(y) = v_1$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Orbit decomposition of the exponent]
$\displaystyle \ell(M) = \sum_{O \in \Orb_G(M)}\bigl(|O|-1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The orbits partition $M$, so $|M| = \sum_O |O|$; every orbit is non-empty, so each $|O|-1$ is an honest subtraction, and summing over the $k$ orbits gives $\sum_O|O| - k = |M|-k$.
\end{proof}

An orbit of size $m$ carries one genuine element and $m-1$ \emph{duplicates}; the meaning-loss exponent counts duplicates, and nothing else.

\section{Logical invariance: only equality is logical}

We now interpret \emph{tuples} over a carrier $\alpha$ with no structure, so the symmetry group is $\Sym(\alpha)$ acting coordinatewise.

\begin{definition}[Kernel]
For $f : \iota \to \alpha$, the \emph{kernel} of $f$ is the equivalence relation $i \equiv_f j \iff f(i)=f(j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transport]\label{thm:transport}
Let $\iota$ be finite and let $f,g : \iota \to \alpha$ have the same kernel. Then there is $\sigma \in \Sym(\alpha)$ with $\sigma(f(i)) = g(i)$ for all $i$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Same-kernel makes $f(i)\mapsto g(i)$ a well-defined injection from the finite set $\ran(f)$ into $\alpha$: well defined since $f(i)=f(j)\Rightarrow g(i)=g(j)$, injective since $g(i)=g(j)\Rightarrow f(i)=f(j)$. It remains to extend this partial injection to a permutation. If $\alpha$ is finite, a partial injection of a finite set into itself extends by counting; if $\alpha$ is infinite, $|\ran(f)| < |\alpha|$ (the range is finite), and a partial injection with domain of strictly smaller cardinality extends to a bijection.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Logical invariance]\label{thm:logical}
Let $\iota$ be finite and $I : (\iota \to \alpha) \to V$. Then $I$ is recoverable with respect to $\Sym(\alpha)$ if and only if $I$ depends only on the kernel: whenever $f(i)=f(j) \iff g(i)=g(j)$ for all $i,j$, we have $I(f)=I(g)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) Same kernel gives, by Theorem~\ref{thm:transport}, a $\sigma$ with $\sigma\cdot f = g$, so $f \sim g$ and orbit constancy applies. ($\Leftarrow$) If $g = \sigma\cdot f$ then $f$ and $g$ have the same kernel, since $\sigma(f(i))=\sigma(f(j))$ iff $f(i)=f(j)$; so $I(f)=I(g)$. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Binary case]
$I : \alpha\times\alpha \to V$ is recoverable iff it is a function of the truth value of $p_1=p_2$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Equality is logical, order is not]
$(x,y)\mapsto[x=y]$ is recoverable; the strict order on $\{0,1,2\}$ is not, since $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$ have identical equality patterns but opposite order values.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness of the arity hypothesis]
Let $\Surj(f)$ assert that $f : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is surjective. Then $\Surj$ is recoverable with respect to the coordinatewise $\Sym(\mathbb{N})$-action but is not kernel-determined; hence Theorem~\ref{thm:logical} fails at infinite arity.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Recoverability: $\sigma$ is a bijection of the codomain, so $f$ is surjective iff $\sigma\cdot f$ is. Failure: $f(n)=2n$ and $g(n)=n$ are both injective, hence share the discrete kernel, but $g$ is surjective and $f$ is not.
\end{proof}

\section{Reconstruction: the theory determines the group}

\begin{definition}[Configurations]
Let $\Cfg(\alpha) := \alpha \to \alpha$ with $\Sym(\alpha)$ acting on values, $(\sigma\cdot f)(a) = \sigma(f(a))$, and write $\mathrm{id}_\alpha$ for the identity configuration.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}
For $G \le \Sym(\alpha)$ let $\Th(G)$ be the set of $G$-recoverable interpretations $\Cfg(\alpha) \to \mathbf{Prop}$. A permutation $\sigma$ \emph{preserves} $I$ when $I(\sigma\cdot f) = I(f)$ for all $f$; for a set $\mathcal{S}$ of interpretations, $\Sym(\mathcal{S})$ is the group of permutations preserving every member.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Membership interpretation]
$\mu_G(f) :\iff \exists g \in G,\ (a \mapsto g(a)) = f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:mu}
$\mu_G \in \Th(G)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $\sigma \in G$: if $f = g \in G$ then $\sigma\cdot f = \sigma g \in G$, and if $\sigma\cdot f = h \in G$ then $f = \sigma^{-1}h \in G$. So $\mu_G$ is orbit-constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Krasner-style reconstruction]\label{thm:krasner}
For $G \le \Sym(\alpha)$ and $\sigma \in \Sym(\alpha)$: $\sigma \in G$ iff $\sigma$ preserves every $I \in \Th(G)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) If $\sigma \in G$ and $I$ is $G$-recoverable then $f \sim_G \sigma\cdot f$, so $I(\sigma\cdot f) = I(f)$.

($\Leftarrow$) By Lemma~\ref{lem:mu}, $\sigma$ preserves $\mu_G$, so $\mu_G(\sigma\cdot\mathrm{id}_\alpha) = \mu_G(\mathrm{id}_\alpha)$, and the latter holds witnessed by $1 \in G$. Hence the tuple $a \mapsto \sigma(a)$ lies in $G$; that element is $\sigma$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
$\Sym(\Th(G)) = G$, and $G \mapsto \Th(G)$ is injective.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Galois connection and strict antitonicity]
$G \le H$ implies $\Th(H)\subseteq\Th(G)$; $\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{T}$ implies $\Sym(\mathcal{T})\le\Sym(\mathcal{S})$; and $G \le \Sym(\mathcal{S}) \iff \mathcal{S}\subseteq\Th(G)$. Moreover $G < H$ implies $\Th(H)\subsetneq\Th(G)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Antitonicity and the adjunction unwind on both sides to ``every $g \in G$ preserves every $I \in \mathcal{S}$''. For strictness, an equality of theories would force $H=G$ by injectivity.
\end{proof}

Thus the recoverability boundary is an intrinsic invariant of structural truth, not an artefact of a chosen group presentation: more symmetry means strictly fewer meanings, with no ties.

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{Algorithm A (orbit partition).} Given a finite carrier $M$ and generators of $G$, compute the orbit partition by union--find over the generator action: for each generator $g$ and each $x$, union $x$ with $g\cdot x$. Cost $O(|M|\,|S|\,\alpha(|M|))$ for $|S|$ generators. Output $\#\Orb$, hence $\ell(M)$.

\paragraph{Algorithm B (recoverability test and recovery).} Given $I$ and the orbit partition, $I$ is recoverable iff constant on each block; the unique recovery sends each block to that common value. Cost $O(|M|)$ after Algorithm A.

\paragraph{Algorithm C (orbit normal form).} Given an invariant $S$, repeatedly pick $x \in S$, emit $\Orb_G(x)$, and replace $S$ by $S \setminus \Orb_G(x)$. This terminates in at most $\#\Orb$ rounds and yields the unique representation of $S$ as a disjoint union of orbits --- the constructive content of Theorem~\ref{thm:countgen}, making the finite classification effective.

\section{Applications}

\textbf{Database genericity.} A query is generic when invariant under renaming of domain elements; descent characterises the annotations that survive renaming, and $\ell$ quantifies how much a schema with symmetry destroys, additively over independent relations.

\textbf{Gauge invariance.} Physically meaningful quantities are exactly those recoverable from the gauge orbit space; the collision theorem says a gauge-dependent quantity is not an observable, and universality says the gauge quotient is the finest observable.

\textbf{Equivariant learning.} A $G$-equivariant model can express only orbit-constant functions of its input; Theorem~\ref{thm:count} gives the exact hypothesis-class size $|V|^{\#\Orb}$, and $\ell$ is an architecture-independent bound on the expressivity cost of symmetry, vanishing exactly on rigid inputs.

\textbf{Logicality.} Theorem~\ref{thm:logical} is the permutation-invariance criterion for logical notions with a provably sharp hypothesis.

\textbf{Combinatorial enumeration.} The Burnside bridge is a semantic reading of the orbit-counting lemma: counting colourings up to symmetry is counting recoverable interpretations.

\section{Discussion}

The original conjecture bundled three claims, and disentangling them yields the following. The conjunction was redundant, so the real content was always about definability alone. The general statement is a theorem in the right language: recoverability is precisely definability in the maximal invariant language, with no hypotheses. Finiteness is exactly what makes that syntax finitely presented --- on finite models the maximal language is generated by orbit predicates, and those predicates are provably necessary, while on infinite models a natural bounded language misses recoverable interpretations, parity being the witness.

The quantitative theory is the unexpected residue. Having settled the qualitative question, counting produced an invariant that was not part of the original problem: $\ell(M) = |M| - \#\Orb(M)$, additive, vanishing exactly on rigid models, and equal to the duplicate count $\sum_O(|O|-1)$. Extensivity, a sharp vanishing criterion and a local decomposition are the signature of a well-behaved structural invariant.

Finally, the theory is self-determining: the reconstruction theorem shows the boundary does not depend on a presentation of the symmetry group, since the group is recoverable from the theory it induces.

\section{Future directions}

\textbf{Presentable invariant languages beyond the finite.} Between the bounded language $\mathcal{F}$ (too weak) and the maximal $\mathcal{O}$ (not finitely presented), which invariant languages on infinite carriers capture recoverability? For oligomorphic groups --- finitely many orbits on $n$-tuples for each $n$ --- a counting language over orbits of tuples should suffice, giving an infinite analogue of the finite collapse.

\textbf{A continuous meaning-loss exponent.} For a compact group acting on a manifold, $\ell$ should become $\dim M - \dim(M/G)$, the generic orbit dimension. Do additivity, rigidity and orbit decomposition survive, and does a measure-theoretic version compute an entropy?

\textbf{Intermediate arities.} Logical invariance holds at finite arity and fails at $\aleph_0$. For a carrier of cardinality $\kappa$ one expects the classification to hold below $\kappa$ and fail at $\kappa$, since transport fails exactly when the tuple's range can exhaust the carrier.

\textbf{Effective reconstruction.} Reconstruction is non-constructive, via the membership interpretation. For finite carriers, how many interpretations must be tested to pin down $G$, and what is the complexity of reconstruction from a bounded sample?

\textbf{Meaning loss under products and quotients.} Additivity handles disjoint unions. What is $\ell(M\times N)$ for the diagonal action, and how does $\ell$ behave under passing to a subgroup or quotient of the acting group? A subgroup can only refine orbits, so $\ell$ is monotone decreasing in the group; quantifying that monotonicity would refine the Galois picture.

\section{Conclusion}

Structure sees its elements only up to symmetry, and this simple fact has an exact theory. An external meaning survives exactly when it is constant on symmetry classes, in which case it survives in exactly one way, and the symmetry-class map is the universal survivor. Whether survivors can also be \emph{expressed} depends on the language: in the largest invariant language, expressibility and survival coincide with no hypotheses; in bounded languages on infinite carriers they diverge, with parity as witness; on finite carriers everything collapses into a single equivalence whose syntax is Boolean combinations of orbit predicates, and that syntax is necessary. The amount of meaning destroyed is a single natural number $\ell(M) = |M| - \#\Orb(M)$: additive over disjoint unions, zero exactly on rigid structures, equal to the number of duplicate elements inside orbits. Over a structureless carrier, the surviving relations of finite arity are precisely those built from equality. And the whole boundary is intrinsic: the symmetry group is itself recoverable from the meanings it permits.

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]          # permutation of range(n) given as an image tuple
Orbit = FrozenSet[int]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permutation-group utilities
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def identity(n: int) -> Perm:
    """The identity permutation of {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return tuple(range(n))


def compose(sigma: Perm, tau: Perm) -> Perm:
    """The permutation (sigma . tau), i.e. first tau then sigma."""
    return tuple(sigma[tau[i]] for i in range(len(tau)))


def generated_group(n: int, generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """Close a set of generators under composition: the subgroup they generate.

    Breadth-first closure; the group of a small model is tiny in practice.
    """
    group: Set[Perm] = {identity(n)}
    frontier: List[Perm] = [identity(n)]
    while frontier:
        new_frontier: List[Perm] = []
        for g in frontier:
            for s in generators:
                h = compose(s, g)
                if h not in group:
                    group.add(h)
                    new_frontier.append(h)
        frontier = new_frontier
    return sorted(group)


def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All n! permutations of {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return sorted(permutations(range(n)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm A: orbit partition by union-find over the generator action
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def orbit_partition(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """The partition of {0,...,n-1} into orbits of the given group.

    Union-find over the action of every group element; O(n |G| a(n)).
    """
    parent: List[int] = list(range(n))

    def find(x: int) -> int:
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def union(x: int, y: int) -> None:
        rx, ry = find(x), find(y)
        if rx != ry:
            parent[max(rx, ry)] = min(rx, ry)

    for g in group:
        for x in range(n):
            union(x, g[x])

    buckets: Dict[int, Set[int]] = {}
    for x in range(n):
        buckets.setdefault(find(x), set()).add(x)
    return sorted((frozenset(b) for b in buckets.values()), key=lambda o: min(o))


def num_orbits(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """The number of orbits of the group on {0,...,n-1}."""
    return len(orbit_partition(n, group))


def meaning_loss(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """The meaning-loss exponent L(M) = |M| - #orbits."""
    return n - num_orbits(n, group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm B: recoverability test and unique recovery
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_recoverable(interp: Sequence[object], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> bool:
    """Orbit Descent: I is recoverable iff it is constant on every orbit."""
    return all(len({interp[x] for x in orbit}) == 1 for orbit in orbits)


def recover(interp: Sequence[object], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> Dict[Orbit, object]:
    """The unique function on the orbit space inducing a recoverable I."""
    if not is_recoverable(interp, orbits):
        raise ValueError("interpretation is not recoverable: it collides on an orbit")
    return {orbit: interp[min(orbit)] for orbit in orbits}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm C: orbit normal form for an invariant set
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_invariant(subset: Set[int], group: Sequence[Perm]) -> bool:
    """Closure of a subset under the group action."""
    return all(g[x] in subset for g in group for x in subset)


def orbit_normal_form(subset: Set[int], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """Peel orbits off an invariant set one at a time (finite completeness).

    Returns the unique decomposition of the set as a disjoint union of orbits;
    raises if the set is not invariant.
    """
    remaining = set(subset)
    pieces: List[Orbit] = []
    while remaining:
        x = min(remaining)
        orbit = next(o for o in orbits if x in o)
        if not orbit <= remaining:
            raise ValueError("set is not invariant: it splits an orbit")
        pieces.append(orbit)
        remaining -= orbit
    return pieces


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graphs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Graph = Tuple[int, FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]]   # (#vertices, set of edges)


def make_graph(n: int, edges: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Graph:
    """A simple graph on {0,...,n-1}."""
    return (n, frozenset(frozenset(e) for e in edges))


def automorphism_group(graph: Graph) -> List[Perm]:
    """All adjacency-preserving permutations of the vertex set (brute force)."""
    n, edges = graph
    out: List[Perm] = []
    for sigma in permutations(range(n)):
        if frozenset(frozenset({sigma[a], sigma[b]}) for a, b in (tuple(e) for e in edges)) == edges:
            out.append(tuple(sigma))
    return sorted(out)


def degrees(graph: Graph) -> List[int]:
    """The vertex-degree interpretation of a graph."""
    n, edges = graph
    return [sum(1 for e in edges if v in e) for v in range(n)]


def path_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The path 0 - 1 - ... - (n-1)."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, i + 1) for i in range(n - 1)])


def cycle_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The cycle 0 - 1 - ... - (n-1) - 0."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, (i + 1) % n) for i in range(n)])


def complete_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The complete graph on n vertices."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)])


def disjoint_union(g1: Graph, g2: Graph) -> Graph:
    """The disjoint union of two graphs, relabelling the second block."""
    n1, e1 = g1
    n2, e2 = g2
    shifted = [tuple(v + n1 for v in e) for e in e2]
    return make_graph(n1 + n2, [tuple(e) for e in e1] + shifted)


def rigid_graph() -> Graph:
    """A smallest asymmetric graph: 6 vertices, trivial automorphism group."""
    return make_graph(6, [(0, 2), (0, 3), (0, 5), (1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 3)])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models:  a carrier together with a group acting on it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Model = Tuple[int, List[Perm]]     # (carrier size, group of symmetries)


def model_of_graph(graph: Graph) -> Model:
    """The model given by a graph and its automorphism group."""
    return (graph[0], automorphism_group(graph))


def model_sum(m1: Model, m2: Model) -> Model:
    """The disjoint union of two models, acted on componentwise.

    This is the setting of the additivity theorem: the group acts on each
    summand separately, so no symmetry mixes the two blocks.
    """
    n1, g1 = m1
    n2, g2 = m2
    combined = [tuple(list(a) + [n1 + b for b in t]) for a in g1 for t in g2]
    return (n1 + n2, sorted(set(combined)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brute-force counting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def count_all_interpretations(n: int, value_count: int) -> int:
    """|V|^|M|: the total number of external interpretations."""
    return value_count ** n


def count_recoverable_bruteforce(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm], value_count: int) -> int:
    """Enumerate every interpretation and count the recoverable ones."""
    orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
    return sum(1 for I in product(range(value_count), repeat=n) if is_recoverable(I, orbits))


def fixed_point_sum(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """sum over g in G of |Fix(g)|, the total number of fixed points."""
    return sum(sum(1 for x in range(n) if g[x] == x) for g in group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tuple interpretations: kernels and logical invariance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kernel(tup: Sequence[int]) -> FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]]:
    """The equality pattern of a tuple: which coordinates coincide."""
    return frozenset((i, j) for i in range(len(tup)) for j in range(len(tup)) if tup[i] == tup[j])


def is_kernel_determined(interp: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], object],
                         carrier: int, arity: int) -> bool:
    """Does the interpretation depend only on the equality pattern of the tuple?"""
    seen: Dict[FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]], object] = {}
    for tup in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
        k = kernel(tup)
        v = interp(tup)
        if k in seen and seen[k] != v:
            return False
        seen[k] = v
    return True


def is_perm_recoverable_tuple(interp: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], object],
                              carrier: int, arity: int) -> bool:
    """Is a tuple interpretation constant on orbits of the coordinatewise
    action of the full symmetric group of the carrier?"""
    for sigma in permutations(range(carrier)):
        for tup in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
            if interp(tuple(sigma[x] for x in tup)) != interp(tup):
                return False
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reconstruction: which permutations preserve every recoverable interpretation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def preserving_permutations(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm], value_count: int = 2) -> List[Perm]:
    """All permutations of the carrier preserving every G-recoverable
    interpretation into a value set of the given size.

    Over a finite carrier this already recovers the orbit partition of G, and
    hence the largest group with the same recoverable theory."""
    orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
    recoverables = [I for I in product(range(value_count), repeat=n)
                    if is_recoverable(I, orbits)]
    return sorted(tuple(sigma) for sigma in permutations(range(n))
                  if all(I[sigma[x]] == I[x] for I in recoverables for x in range(n)))

    print(f"  is recoverable: {is_recoverable(indicator, orbits)}")

    print("  in the counting language.")
    print("\nIn the TRIVIAL invariant language (only the empty set and everything),")
    print("  a definable interpretation must have every fibre empty or total, i.e.")
    print("  must be constant.  chi is non-constant, so it is NOT definable there:")
    print(f"  chi constant = {len(set(indicator)) == 1}")
    print("\nHence as soon as a finite structure has two orbits, adding orbit-counting")
    print("modalities strictly increases expressive power.")

def demo_infinite_boundary() -> None:
    rule("9. THE INFINITE BOUNDARY: PARITY IS RECOVERABLE BUT NOT DEFINABLE")
    print("Take the naturals with the TRIVIAL symmetry group.  Indistinguishability")
    print("is then equality, so EVERY interpretation is orbit-constant, hence")
    print("recoverable.  In particular parity is recoverable.")
    print("\nNow take the bounded invariant language of finite-or-cofinite sets.")
    print("Definability there requires each fibre to be finite or cofinite.")
    for n in (10, 100, 1000, 10000):
        evens = sum(1 for k in range(n) if k % 2 == 0)
        odds = n - evens
        print(f"  among the first {n:>5} naturals: {evens:>5} even, {odds:>5} odd")
    print("\nBoth counts grow without bound (k -> 2k injects into the evens and")
    print("k -> 2k+1 into the odds), so the fibre of parity is neither finite nor")
    print("cofinite.  Parity is recoverable but undefinable: on infinite carriers,")
    print("orbit constancy is STRICTLY WEAKER than definability in a bounded language.")
    print("\nNote the contrast: in the MAXIMAL invariant language (all invariant sets)")
    print("the evens are invariant here, so parity is definable there.  What fails is")
    print("expressive capacity, not invariance -- and on finite carriers no such gap")
    print("can open, since a finite invariant algebra is already all invariant sets.")

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]          # permutation of range(n) given as an image tuple
Orbit = FrozenSet[int]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permutation-group utilities
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def identity(n: int) -> Perm:
    """The identity permutation of {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return tuple(range(n))


def compose(sigma: Perm, tau: Perm) -> Perm:
    """The permutation (sigma . tau), i.e. first tau then sigma."""
    return tuple(sigma[tau[i]] for i in range(len(tau)))


def generated_group(n: int, generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """Close a set of generators under composition: the subgroup they generate.

    Breadth-first closure; the group of a small model is tiny in practice.
    """
    group: Set[Perm] = {identity(n)}
    frontier: List[Perm] = [identity(n)]
    while frontier:
        new_frontier: List[Perm] = []
        for g in frontier:
            for s in generators:
                h = compose(s, g)
                if h not in group:
                    group.add(h)
                    new_frontier.append(h)
        frontier = new_frontier
    return sorted(group)


def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All n! permutations of {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return sorted(permutations(range(n)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm A: orbit partition by union-find over the generator action
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def orbit_partition(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """The partition of {0,...,n-1} into orbits of the given group.

    Union-find over the action of every group element; O(n |G| a(n)).
    """
    parent: List[int] = list(range(n))

    def find(x: int) -> int:
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def union(x: int, y: int) -> None:
        rx, ry = find(x), find(y)
        if rx != ry:
            parent[max(rx, ry)] = min(rx, ry)

    for g in group:
        for x in range(n):
            union(x, g[x])

    buckets: Dict[int, Set[int]] = {}
    for x in range(n):
        buckets.setdefault(find(x), set()).add(x)
    return sorted((frozenset(b) for b in buckets.values()), key=lambda o: min(o))


def num_orbits(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """The number of orbits of the group on {0,...,n-1}."""
    return len(orbit_partition(n, group))


def meaning_loss(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """The meaning-loss exponent L(M) = |M| - #orbits."""
    return n - num_orbits(n, group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm B: recoverability test and unique recovery
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_recoverable(interp: Sequence[object], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> bool:
    """Orbit Descent: I is recoverable iff it is constant on every orbit."""
    return all(len({interp[x] for x in orbit}) == 1 for orbit in orbits)


def recover(interp: Sequence[object], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> Dict[Orbit, object]:
    """The unique function on the orbit space inducing a recoverable I."""
    if not is_recoverable(interp, orbits):
        raise ValueError("interpretation is not recoverable: it collides on an orbit")
    return {orbit: interp[min(orbit)] for orbit in orbits}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Algorithm C: orbit normal form for an invariant set
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_invariant(subset: Set[int], group: Sequence[Perm]) -> bool:
    """Closure of a subset under the group action."""
    return all(g[x] in subset for g in group for x in subset)


def orbit_normal_form(subset: Set[int], orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """Peel orbits off an invariant set one at a time (finite completeness).

    Returns the unique decomposition of the set as a disjoint union of orbits;
    raises if the set is not invariant.
    """
    remaining = set(subset)
    pieces: List[Orbit] = []
    while remaining:
        x = min(remaining)
        orbit = next(o for o in orbits if x in o)
        if not orbit <= remaining:
            raise ValueError("set is not invariant: it splits an orbit")
        pieces.append(orbit)
        remaining -= orbit
    return pieces


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graphs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Graph = Tuple[int, FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]]   # (#vertices, set of edges)


def make_graph(n: int, edges: Iterable[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Graph:
    """A simple graph on {0,...,n-1}."""
    return (n, frozenset(frozenset(e) for e in edges))


def automorphism_group(graph: Graph) -> List[Perm]:
    """All adjacency-preserving permutations of the vertex set (brute force)."""
    n, edges = graph
    out: List[Perm] = []
    for sigma in permutations(range(n)):
        if frozenset(frozenset({sigma[a], sigma[b]}) for a, b in (tuple(e) for e in edges)) == edges:
            out.append(tuple(sigma))
    return sorted(out)


def degrees(graph: Graph) -> List[int]:
    """The vertex-degree interpretation of a graph."""
    n, edges = graph
    return [sum(1 for e in edges if v in e) for v in range(n)]


def path_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The path 0 - 1 - ... - (n-1)."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, i + 1) for i in range(n - 1)])


def cycle_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The cycle 0 - 1 - ... - (n-1) - 0."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, (i + 1) % n) for i in range(n)])


def complete_graph(n: int) -> Graph:
    """The complete graph on n vertices."""
    return make_graph(n, [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)])


def disjoint_union(g1: Graph, g2: Graph) -> Graph:
    """The disjoint union of two graphs, relabelling the second block."""
    n1, e1 = g1
    n2, e2 = g2
    shifted = [tuple(v + n1 for v in e) for e in e2]
    return make_graph(n1 + n2, [tuple(e) for e in e1] + shifted)


def rigid_graph() -> Graph:
    """A smallest asymmetric graph: 6 vertices, trivial automorphism group."""
    return make_graph(6, [(0, 2), (0, 3), (0, 5), (1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 3)])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models:  a carrier together with a group acting on it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Model = Tuple[int, List[Perm]]     # (carrier size, group of symmetries)


def model_of_graph(graph: Graph) -> Model:
    """The model given by a graph and its automorphism group."""
    return (graph[0], automorphism_group(graph))


def model_sum(m1: Model, m2: Model) -> Model:
    """The disjoint union of two models, acted on componentwise.

    This is the setting of the additivity theorem: the group acts on each
    summand separately, so no symmetry mixes the two blocks.
    """
    n1, g1 = m1
    n2, g2 = m2
    combined = [tuple(list(a) + [n1 + b for b in t]) for a in g1 for t in g2]
    return (n1 + n2, sorted(set(combined)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brute-force counting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def count_all_interpretations(n: int, value_count: int) -> int:
    """|V|^|M|: the total number of external interpretations."""
    return value_count ** n


def count_recoverable_bruteforce(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm], value_count: int) -> int:
    """Enumerate every interpretation and count the recoverable ones."""
    orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
    return sum(1 for I in product(range(value_count), repeat=n) if is_recoverable(I, orbits))


def fixed_point_sum(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """sum over g in G of |Fix(g)|, the total number of fixed points."""
    return sum(sum(1 for x in range(n) if g[x] == x) for g in group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tuple interpretations: kernels and logical invariance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kernel(tup: Sequence[int]) -> FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]]:
    """The equality pattern of a tuple: which coordinates coincide."""
    return frozenset((i, j) for i in range(len(tup)) for j in range(len(tup)) if tup[i] == tup[j])


def is_kernel_determined(interp: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], object],
                         carrier: int, arity: int) -> bool:
    """Does the interpretation depend only on the equality pattern of the tuple?"""
    seen: Dict[FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]], object] = {}
    for tup in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
        k = kernel(tup)
        v = interp(tup)
        if k in seen and seen[k] != v:
            return False
        seen[k] = v
    return True


def is_perm_recoverable_tuple(interp: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], object],
                              carrier: int, arity: int) -> bool:
    """Is a tuple interpretation constant on orbits of the coordinatewise
    action of the full symmetric group of the carrier?"""
    for sigma in permutations(range(carrier)):
        for tup in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
            if interp(tuple(sigma[x] for x in tup)) != interp(tup):
                return False
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reconstruction: which permutations preserve every recoverable interpretation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def preserving_permutations(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm], value_count: int = 2) -> List[Perm]:
    """All permutations of the carrier preserving every G-recoverable
    interpretation into a value set of the given size.

    Over a finite carrier this already recovers the orbit partition of G, and
    hence the largest group with the same recoverable theory."""
    orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
    recoverables = [I for I in product(range(value_count), repeat=n)
                    if is_recoverable(I, orbits)]
    return sorted(tuple(sigma) for sigma in permutations(range(n))
                  if all(I[sigma[x]] == I[x] for I in recoverables for x in range(n)))

    print(f"  -> the unique recovery is {[(sorted(o), v) for o, v in recover(deg, orbits).items()]}")

def demo_total_annihilation() -> None:
    rule("2. MAXIMAL SYMMETRY ANNIHILATES MEANING")
    for n in (2, 3, 4):
        group = symmetric_group(n)
        orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
        recoverable = [I for I in product(range(3), repeat=n) if is_recoverable(I, orbits)]
        constants = [I for I in recoverable if len(set(I)) == 1]
        print(f"n = {n}: full symmetric group, {len(orbits)} orbit; "
              f"{len(recoverable)} recoverable interpretations into a 3-element value set, "
              f"all constant = {recoverable == constants}")
    print("\ncomplete graphs realise this: every permutation is an automorphism.")
    for n in (3, 4):
        kn = complete_graph(n)
        print(f"  K_{n}: |Aut| = {len(automorphism_group(kn))} = {n}! , "
              f"orbits = {len(orbit_partition(n, automorphism_group(kn)))}")
    print("\nsmallest meaning collision: the 2-element carrier under all permutations,")
    print("  the identity interpretation I(x) = x assigns different meanings to two")
    print("  indistinguishable elements, so it cannot be recovered:")

    examples: List[Tuple[str, Model]] = [

    for name, (n, group) in examples:
        orbits = orbit_partition(n, group)
        dup = sum(len(o) - 1 for o in orbits)
        print(f"  {name}: sizes {sorted(len(o) for o in orbits)} -> duplicates {dup}, "
              f"L = {n - len(orbits)}, equal = {dup == n - len(orbits)}")


def demo_additivity_and_rigidity() -> None:
    rule("4. ADDITIVITY AND THE RIGIDITY CRITERION")
    print("The symmetry group acts on each summand separately, so no symmetry mixes")
    print("the two blocks -- this is exactly the setting of the additivity theorem.\n")
    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Model, str, Model]] = [
        ("P3", model_of_graph(path_graph(3)), "P3", model_of_graph(path_graph(3))),
        ("P3", model_of_graph(path_graph(3)), "C4", model_of_graph(cycle_graph(4))),
        ("K3", model_of_graph(complete_graph(3)), "P4", model_of_graph(path_graph(4))),
        ("C5", model_of_graph(cycle_graph(5)), "K4", model_of_graph(complete_graph(4))),
        ("K3", model_of_graph(complete_graph(3)), "rigid6",

def demo_infinite_boundary() -> None:
    rule("9. THE INFINITE BOUNDARY: PARITY IS RECOVERABLE BUT NOT DEFINABLE")
    print("Take the naturals with the TRIVIAL symmetry group.  Indistinguishability")
    print("is then equality, so EVERY interpretation is orbit-constant, hence")
    print("recoverable.  In particular parity is recoverable.")
    print("\nNow take the bounded invariant language of finite-or-cofinite sets.")
    print("Definability there requires each fibre to be finite or cofinite.")
    for n in (10, 100, 1000, 10000):
        evens = sum(1 for k in range(n) if k % 2 == 0)
        odds = n - evens
        print(f"  among the first {n:>5} naturals: {evens:>5} even, {odds:>5} odd")
    print("\nBoth counts grow without bound (k -> 2k injects into the evens and")
    print("k -> 2k+1 into the odds), so the fibre of parity is neither finite nor")
    print("cofinite.  Parity is recoverable but undefinable: on infinite carriers,")
    print("orbit constancy is STRICTLY WEAKER than definability in a bounded language.")
    print("\nNote the contrast: in the MAXIMAL invariant language (all invariant sets)")
    print("the evens are invariant here, so parity is definable there.  What fails is")
    print("expressive capacity, not invariance -- and on finite carriers no such gap")
    print("can open, since a finite invariant algebra is already all invariant sets.")

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations, permutations, product
from typing import FrozenSet, Iterator, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
Edges = FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]
Model = Tuple[int, List[Perm]]


def all_graphs(n: int) -> Iterator[Edges]:
    """Every labelled simple graph on n vertices."""
    pairs = list(combinations(range(n), 2))
    for mask in range(1 << len(pairs)):
        yield frozenset(frozenset(pairs[i]) for i in range(len(pairs)) if mask >> i & 1)


def automorphisms(n: int, edges: Edges) -> List[Perm]:
    """Automorphism group of a graph, by brute force over all permutations."""
    return [tuple(s) for s in permutations(range(n))
            if frozenset(frozenset({s[a], s[b]})
                         for a, b in (tuple(e) for e in edges)) == edges]


def orbits_of(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[FrozenSet[int]]:
    """Orbit partition of the carrier under the group."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    out: List[FrozenSet[int]] = []
    for x in range(n):
        if x in seen:
            continue
        orb = frozenset(g[x] for g in group)
        seen |= orb
        out.append(orb)
    return out


def recoverable_count(n: int, orbs: Sequence[FrozenSet[int]], value_count: int) -> int:
    """Brute-force count of orbit-constant interpretations."""
    return sum(1 for I in product(range(value_count), repeat=n)
               if all(len({I[x] for x in o}) == 1 for o in orbs))


def model_sum(m1: Model, m2: Model) -> Model:
    """Disjoint union of two models, acted on componentwise."""
    n1, g1 = m1
    n2, g2 = m2
    return (n1 + n2,
            sorted({tuple(list(a) + [n1 + b for b in t]) for a in g1 for t in g2}))


def census(max_vertices: int = 5, value_count: int = 3) -> None:
    print(f"{'n':>3}{'graphs':>9}{'checked (a)':>13}{'(b)':>7}{'(c)':>7}{'(d)':>7}"
          f"{'max L':>8}{'rigid graphs':>15}")
    print("-" * 69)
    for n in range(1, max_vertices + 1):
        total = ok_a = ok_b = ok_c = ok_d = 0
        max_loss = 0
        rigid = 0
        for edges in all_graphs(n):
            total += 1
            group = automorphisms(n, edges)
            orbs = orbits_of(n, group)
            k = len(orbs)
            loss = n - k
            max_loss = max(max_loss, loss)

            # (a) counting formula, checked against brute force
            if n <= 5 and recoverable_count(n, orbs, value_count) == value_count ** k:
                ok_a += 1

            # (b) orbit decomposition
            if sum(len(o) - 1 for o in orbs) == loss:
                ok_b += 1

            # (c) rigidity criterion, all three readings at once
            is_rigid = all(len(o) == 1 for o in orbs)
            everything_recoverable = (recoverable_count(n, orbs, 2) == 2 ** n)
            if (loss == 0) == is_rigid == everything_recoverable:
                ok_c += 1
            if is_rigid:
                rigid += 1

            # (d) Burnside
            fix_sum = sum(sum(1 for x in range(n) if g[x] == x) for g in group)
            if fix_sum == k * len(group) and 2 ** fix_sum == (2 ** k) ** len(group):
                ok_d += 1

        print(f"{n:>3}{total:>9}{ok_a:>13}{ok_b:>7}{ok_c:>7}{ok_d:>7}"
              f"{max_loss:>8}{rigid:>15}")
    print("\nEvery column equals the graph count: all four facts hold for every graph.")
    print("The last column shows that the only rigid graph on at most five vertices is")
    print("the single-vertex graph: every larger graph has two vertices some symmetry")
    print("exchanges, hence destroys meaning.  The smallest rigid graph beyond that has")
    print("six vertices, for instance the one with edges 02, 03, 05, 12, 14, 23.")


def additivity_check(max_vertices: int = 4) -> None:
    print("\nADDITIVITY over componentwise disjoint unions")
    models: List[Model] = []
    for n in range(1, max_vertices + 1):
        for edges in all_graphs(n):
            models.append((n, automorphisms(n, edges)))
    checked = failures = 0
    for m1 in models:
        for m2 in models:
            l1 = m1[0] - len(orbits_of(*m1))
            l2 = m2[0] - len(orbits_of(*m2))
            msum = model_sum(m1, m2)
            lsum = msum[0] - len(orbits_of(*msum))
            checked += 1
            if lsum != l1 + l2:
                failures += 1
    print(f"  pairs checked: {checked}, additivity failures: {failures}")
    print("  L(M + N) = L(M) + L(N) holds in every case: the exponent is extensive.")

Over a carrier with no structure at all, every permutation is a symmetry, and an
interpretation of tuples is recoverable from structural truth exactly when it
depends only on the kernel of the tuple -- the pattern of coincidences among the
coordinates.  This script enumerates *all* relations of small arity on a small
carrier and confirms the classification exactly:

  * the number of recoverable relations of arity k is 2 raised to the number of
    kernel classes, i.e. to the number of set partitions of the k coordinates
    (a Bell number), and is completely independent of the size of the carrier
    once the carrier is large enough to realise every partition;
  * the recoverable relations are precisely those definable from equality;
  * equality is recoverable, and strict order is not.

It also displays the surviving relations explicitly, as Boolean combinations of
equalities between coordinates.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Tuple

Tup = Tuple[int, ...]


def kernel(t: Tup) -> Tup:
    """Canonical form of the equality pattern: rename by first occurrence."""
    seen: Dict[int, int] = {}
    out: List[int] = []
    for x in t:
        if x not in seen:
            seen[x] = len(seen)
        out.append(seen[x])
    return tuple(out)


def kernel_classes(carrier: int, arity: int) -> Dict[Tup, List[Tup]]:
    """Group all tuples by their kernel."""
    classes: Dict[Tup, List[Tup]] = {}
    for t in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
        classes.setdefault(kernel(t), []).append(t)
    return classes


def bell_number(k: int) -> int:
    """The number of set partitions of a k-element set (Bell triangle)."""
    row = [1]
    for _ in range(k):
        nxt = [row[-1]]
        for x in row:
            nxt.append(nxt[-1] + x)
        row = nxt
    return row[0]


def is_permutation_invariant(rel: FrozenSet[Tup], carrier: int, arity: int) -> bool:
    """Is the relation closed under the coordinatewise action of every permutation?"""
    for s in permutations(range(carrier)):
        for t in product(range(carrier), repeat=arity):
            if (t in rel) != (tuple(s[x] for x in t) in rel):
                return False
    return True


def is_kernel_determined(rel: FrozenSet[Tup], classes: Dict[Tup, List[Tup]]) -> bool:
    """Is the relation constant on every kernel class?"""
    for members in classes.values():
        vals = {t in rel for t in members}
        if len(vals) > 1:
            return False
    return True


def describe(pattern: Tup) -> str:
    """Render a kernel as a readable equality pattern, e.g. 'x = z, y separate'."""
    names = "xyzw"
    blocks: Dict[int, List[str]] = {}
    for i, b in enumerate(pattern):
        blocks.setdefault(b, []).append(names[i])
    return " | ".join(" = ".join(g) for g in blocks.values())


def census(carrier: int, arity: int, exhaustive_limit: int = 1 << 22) -> None:
    classes = kernel_classes(carrier, arity)
    tuples = list(product(range(carrier), repeat=arity))
    total = 1 << len(tuples)
    print(f"\ncarrier of size {carrier}, arity {arity}: "
          f"{len(tuples)} tuples, {total} relations in all")
    print(f"  kernel classes ({len(classes)}): "
          + ";  ".join(describe(p) for p in sorted(classes)))
    predicted = 2 ** len(classes)
    print(f"  predicted number of recoverable relations: 2^{len(classes)} = {predicted}"
          f"   (Bell number of {arity} is {bell_number(arity)})")

    if total <= exhaustive_limit:
        found = 0
        agree = True
        for mask in range(total):
            rel = frozenset(tuples[i] for i in range(len(tuples)) if mask >> i & 1)
            kd = is_kernel_determined(rel, classes)
            if kd:
                found += 1
            if carrier <= 3 and arity <= 2:
                if kd != is_permutation_invariant(rel, carrier, arity):
                    agree = False
        print(f"  brute-force count of kernel-determined relations: {found}"
              f"   match = {found == predicted}")
        if carrier <= 3 and arity <= 2:
            print(f"  kernel-determined and permutation-invariant agree on every one of"
                  f" the {total} relations: {agree}")
    else:
        print("  (too many relations to enumerate exhaustively at this size)")


def named_examples(carrier: int = 4) -> None:
    print("\nNamed binary relations on a bare carrier:")
    tests: List[Tuple[str, Callable[[int, int], bool]]] = [
        ("equality        x = y", lambda x, y: x == y),
        ("distinctness    x != y", lambda x, y: x != y),
        ("strict order    x < y", lambda x, y: x < y),
        ("weak order      x <= y", lambda x, y: x <= y),
        ("constant true", lambda x, y: True),
        ("constant false", lambda x, y: False),
        ("first is zero   x = 0", lambda x, y: x == 0),
    ]
    classes = kernel_classes(carrier, 2)
    for name, f in tests:
        rel = frozenset((x, y) for x in range(carrier) for y in range(carrier) if f(x, y))
        kd = is_kernel_determined(rel, classes)

        print(f"  {name:26} kernel-determined={str(kd):5} "
              f"permutation-invariant={str(pi):5}  ->  {verdict}")
    print("\n  Exactly four binary relations survive on a bare set: the empty relation,")

def orbit_partition(n: int, generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """Partition {0,...,n-1} into orbits of the group generated by `generators`.

def is_invariant(subset: Set[int], generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> bool:
    """A subset is invariant iff closed under every generator."""
    return all(g[x] in subset for g in generators for x in subset)


def orbit_normal_form(subset: Set[int],
                      orbits: Sequence[Orbit]) -> List[Orbit]:
    """Decompose an invariant set into a disjoint union of orbits.

        pieces.append(orbit)
        remaining -= orbit
    return pieces

    """Render an orbit normal form as a disjunction of orbit predicates."""
    if not pieces:

    """The subgroup of the symmetric group generated by the given permutations."""

Two panels.

inclusion, the number of external interpretations into a three-element value set
that are recoverable from structural truth.  The count is |V| raised to the
number of orbits, so it collapses as symmetry grows: more symmetry means
strictly fewer recoverable meanings.

total number of interpretations splits as (recoverable count) x (loss factor

vertical gap between the two bars is exactly the exponent, in units of log|V|.

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations
from typing import FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


def close_group(n: int, generators: Sequence[Perm]) -> List[Perm]:
    """The subgroup generated by the given permutations."""
    identity: Perm = tuple(range(n))
    group: Set[Perm] = {identity}
    frontier: List[Perm] = [identity]
    while frontier:
        nxt: List[Perm] = []
        for g in frontier:
            for s in generators:
                h = tuple(s[g[i]] for i in range(n))
                if h not in group:
                    group.add(h)
                    nxt.append(h)
        frontier = nxt
    return sorted(group)


def orbit_count(n: int, group: Sequence[Perm]) -> int:
    """Number of orbits of the group on {0,...,n-1}."""
    seen: Set[int] = set()
    count = 0
    for x in range(n):
        if x in seen:
            continue
        seen |= {g[x] for g in group}
        count += 1
    return count


def automorphisms(n: int, edges: FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]) -> List[Perm]:
    """Automorphism group of a simple graph, by brute force."""
    return [tuple(s) for s in permutations(range(n))
            if frozenset(frozenset({s[a], s[b]})
                         for a, b in (tuple(e) for e in edges)) == edges]


def main() -> None:
    value_count = 3
    n = 4

    chain: List[Tuple[str, List[Perm]]] = [
        ("trivial", close_group(n, [])),
        (r"$\langle (01)\rangle$", close_group(n, [(1, 0, 2, 3)])),
        (r"$\langle (01),(23)\rangle$", close_group(n, [(1, 0, 2, 3), (0, 1, 3, 2)])),
        (r"$\langle (0123)\rangle$", close_group(n, [(1, 2, 3, 0)])),
        (r"dihedral $D_4$", close_group(n, [(1, 2, 3, 0), (0, 3, 2, 1)])),

    counts = [value_count ** orbit_count(n, g) for _, g in chain]
    losses = [n - orbit_count(n, g) for _, g in chain]

    bars = ax1.bar(range(len(chain)), counts, color="#3a6ea5", edgecolor="black")

    ax1.set_ylim(0, max(counts) * 1.28)

    def edges(pairs: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]) -> FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]:
        return frozenset(frozenset(p) for p in pairs)

    structures: List[Tuple[str, int, FrozenSet[FrozenSet[int]]]] = [
        (r"$P_3$", 3, edges([(0, 1), (1, 2)])),
        (r"$P_4$", 4, edges([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)])),
        (r"$K_{1,3}$", 4, edges([(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3)])),

    names, rec, total, exps = [], [], [], []

        total.append(value_count ** size)

    ax2.set_yscale("log")
    ax2.set_ylim(1, max(total) * 6)
    ax2.set_xticks(idx)
    ax2.set_xticklabels(names, fontsize=10)
    ax2.set_ylabel("count (log scale)")
    ax2.set_title("The meaning-loss factorisation\n"
                  r"$|V|^{|M|} = |V|^{\#\mathrm{orbits}} \cdot |V|^{\ell(M)}$"
                  "   (the gap is the exponent)", fontsize=11)
    ax2.legend(fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    ax2.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("symmetry_versus_meaning.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote symmetry_versus_meaning.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"use strict";

/* ---------- preset structures: vertices, edges, drawing layout ---------- */
const PRESETS = {
  "Path  0 – 1 – 2": {
    n: 3, edges: [[0,1],[1,2]],
    pos: [[90,170],[230,170],[370,170]]
  },
  "Path  0 – 1 – 2 – 3": {
    n: 4, edges: [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3]],

  },
  "Star  K(1,3)": {

  },
  "Cycle  C4": {
