    pos: [[230,55],[365,170],[230,285],[95,170]]
  },
  "Complete  K4": {
    n: 4, edges: [[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[1,2],[1,3],[2,3]],
    pos: [[230,55],[365,170],[230,285],[95,170]]
  },
  "Cycle  C5": {
    n: 5, edges: [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[4,0]],
    pos: [[230,50],[365,150],[313,285],[147,285],[95,150]]
  },
  "Two disjoint edges": {
    n: 4, edges: [[0,1],[2,3]],
    pos: [[130,80],[130,260],[330,80],[330,260]]
  },
  "Path + triangle": {
    n: 6, edges: [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4],[4,5],[5,3]],
    pos: [[70,90],[70,180],[70,270],[300,80],[400,240],[210,240]]
  },
  "A rigid graph": {
    n: 6, edges: [[0,2],[0,3],[0,5],[1,2],[1,4],[2,3]],
    pos: [[230,50],[360,120],[360,240],[230,300],[100,240],[100,120]]
  }
};

const MEANINGS = ["#6ba8ff", "#ffcf5c", "#b98cff"];
const ORBIT_COLORS = ["#3ddc97","#ff8fab","#ffd166","#7fd7ff","#c792ea","#f4a261"];

let current = null;      // {n, edges, pos, group, orbits}
let painting = [];       // meaning index per vertex

/* ---------- permutation utilities ---------- */
function* permutations(n){
  const a = Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>i);
  const c = new Array(n).fill(0);
  yield a.slice();
  let i = 0;
  while(i < n){
    if(c[i] < i){
      const j = (i % 2 === 0) ? 0 : c[i];
      [a[i],a[j]] = [a[j],a[i]];
      yield a.slice();
      c[i]++; i = 0;
    } else { c[i] = 0; i++; }
  }
}

function edgeKey(a,b){ return a < b ? a+"-"+b : b+"-"+a; }

function automorphisms(n, edges){
  const set = new Set(edges.map(([a,b]) => edgeKey(a,b)));
  const out = [];
  for(const s of permutations(n)){
    let ok = true;
    for(const [a,b] of edges){
      if(!set.has(edgeKey(s[a], s[b]))){ ok = false; break; }
    }
    if(ok) out.push(s.slice());
  }
  return out;
}

function orbitsOf(n, group){
  const seen = new Set(), out = [];
  for(let x = 0; x < n; x++){
    if(seen.has(x)) continue;
    const orb = new Set(group.map(g => g[x]));
    orb.forEach(v => seen.add(v));
    out.push([...orb].sort((p,q)=>p-q));
  }
  return out;
}

function fixedPointSum(n, group){
  let s = 0;
  for(const g of group) for(let x = 0; x < n; x++) if(g[x] === x) s++;
  return s;
}

/* ---------- the mathematics on display ---------- */
function collisions(){
  const bad = [];
  for(const orb of current.orbits){
    const base = orb[0];
    for(const v of orb.slice(1)){
      if(painting[v] !== painting[base]) bad.push([base, v]);
    }
  }
  return bad;
}

function orbitIndexOf(v){
  return current.orbits.findIndex(o => o.includes(v));
}

/* ---------- rendering ---------- */
function render(){
  const svg = document.getElementById("canvas");
  const bad = collisions();
  const badVerts = new Set(bad.flat());
  let html = "";

  for(const [a,b] of current.edges){
    const [x1,y1] = current.pos[a], [x2,y2] = current.pos[b];
    html += `<line x1="${x1}" y1="${y1}" x2="${x2}" y2="${y2}"
             stroke="#4b5b7d" stroke-width="2.6"/>`;
  }
  for(const [base, v] of bad){
    const [x1,y1] = current.pos[base], [x2,y2] = current.pos[v];
    html += `<line x1="${x1}" y1="${y1}" x2="${x2}" y2="${y2}"
             stroke="#ff6b6b" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-dasharray="7 6" opacity="0.85"/>`;
  }
  for(let v = 0; v < current.n; v++){
    const [x,y] = current.pos[v];
    const ring = ORBIT_COLORS[orbitIndexOf(v) % ORBIT_COLORS.length];
    const fill = MEANINGS[painting[v]];
    const pulse = badVerts.has(v) ? ` stroke-dasharray="4 3"` : "";
    html += `<g class="vtx" data-v="${v}" style="cursor:pointer">
      <circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="21" fill="${fill}" stroke="${ring}"
              stroke-width="5"${pulse}/>
      <text x="${x}" y="${y+5}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14"
            font-weight="700" fill="#0d1526">${v}</text></g>`;
  }
  svg.innerHTML = html;
  svg.querySelectorAll(".vtx").forEach(g => {
    g.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const v = +g.dataset.v;
      painting[v] = (painting[v] + 1) % MEANINGS.length;
      render();
    });
  });

  const n = current.n, k = current.orbits.length, L = n - k;
  const dup = current.orbits.reduce((s,o) => s + o.length - 1, 0);
  const all = Math.pow(3, n), rec = Math.pow(3, k), fac = Math.pow(3, L);
  const fixSum = fixedPointSum(n, current.group);
  const R = Math.pow(2, k), G = current.group.length;
  const burnOK = (fixSum === k * G);   // equivalent to 2^fixSum = R^G

  document.getElementById("n").textContent = n;
  document.getElementById("aut").textContent = G;
  document.getElementById("orb").textContent =
      k + "  " + current.orbits.map(o => "{" + o.join(",") + "}").join(" ");
  document.getElementById("loss").textContent = L;
  document.getElementById("dup").textContent = dup + (dup === L ? "  ✓ equals ℓ" : "");
  document.getElementById("all").textContent = all;
  document.getElementById("rec").textContent = rec;
  document.getElementById("fac").textContent = fac + "  (= " + all + " / " + rec + ")";
  document.getElementById("fix").textContent = fixSum;
  document.getElementById("burn").textContent =
      "2^" + fixSum + " = " + R + "^" + G + (burnOK ? "  ✓" : "  ✗");

  const verdict = document.getElementById("verdict");
  if(bad.length === 0){
    const recovery = current.orbits
      .map(o => "{" + o.join(",") + "} ↦ " + "ABC"[painting[o[0]]]).join("  ·  ");
    verdict.innerHTML = `<span class="ok">✓ Recoverable.</span> This painting is constant
      on every symmetry class, so structural truth reconstructs it — and the
      reconstruction is unique:<br><span style="color:#cfe0ff">${recovery}</span>`;
  } else {
    const [a,b] = bad[0];
    verdict.innerHTML = `<span class="no">✗ Meaning collision.</span> Vertices
      <b>${a}</b> and <b>${b}</b> are structurally indistinguishable — a symmetry
      carries one to the other — yet you gave them different meanings
      (${"ABC"[painting[a]]} vs ${"ABC"[painting[b]]}). No function on the symmetry
      classes can reproduce this painting.`;
  }

  const nf = current.orbits.map((o,i) => "O" + (i+1)).join(" ∪ ");
  document.getElementById("normalform").innerHTML =
    `<b>Orbit normal form.</b> Every predicate this structure can express is a Boolean
     combination of its ${k} orbit predicates ${nf}: there are exactly
     2<sup>${k}</sup> = ${Math.pow(2,k)} structurally expressible properties of a vertex,
     out of 2<sup>${n}</sup> = ${Math.pow(2,n)} properties in total.`;
}

/* ---------- controls ---------- */
function load(name){
  const p = PRESETS[name];
  const group = automorphisms(p.n, p.edges);
  current = {n:p.n, edges:p.edges, pos:p.pos, group, orbits: orbitsOf(p.n, group)};
  painting = new Array(p.n).fill(0);
  render();
}

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const sel = document.getElementById("preset");
  Object.keys(PRESETS).forEach(k => {
    const opt = document.createElement("option");
    opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k; sel.appendChild(opt);
  });
  sel.addEventListener("change", () => load(sel.value));
  document.getElementById("reset").addEventListener("click", () => {
    painting = new Array(current.n).fill(0); render();
  });
  document.getElementById("random").addEventListener("click", () => {
    painting = painting.map(() => Math.floor(Math.random()*MEANINGS.length)); render();
  });
  document.getElementById("project").addEventListener("click", () => {
    // Replace the painting by the recoverable one agreeing with it on a
    // representative of each class: this is the closest orbit-constant painting.
    for(const orb of current.orbits){
      const v = painting[orb[0]];
      orb.forEach(x => { painting[x] = v; });
    }
    render();
  });
  load(Object.keys(PRESETS)[0]);
});
</script>

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Only Equality Is Logical</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    Over a bare set with no structure at all, every permutation is a symmetry. Which
    relations can such a set carry? Build one by hand and find out. The answer, in a
    sentence: <em>exactly those that depend only on which coordinates are equal.</em>
  </p>

  <div class="card">
    <h2>1 · Build a relation on a bare set</h2>
    <div class="row">
      <label>carrier size
        <select id="carrier"><option>3</option><option>4</option></select>
      </label>
      <label>arity
        <select id="arity"><option>2</option><option>3</option></select>
      </label>
      <select id="preset">
        <option value="custom">— preset —</option>
        <option value="eq">equality  x = y</option>
        <option value="neq">distinctness  x ≠ y</option>
        <option value="lt">strict order  x < y</option>
        <option value="first">first coordinate is 0</option>
        <option value="alldist">all coordinates distinct</option>
        <option value="cyc">cyclic successor  y = x+1 mod n</option>
        <option value="empty">always false</option>
      </select>
      <button id="clear">Clear</button>
      <button id="fix">Repair to nearest logical relation</button>
    </div>
    <div id="classes"></div>
    <div class="hint">Click a tuple to toggle whether the relation holds of it. Tuples are
      grouped by their <b>kernel</b>: their pattern of coincidences, i.e. which
      coordinates are equal to which. A red outline marks a tuple that disagrees with
      another tuple of the same kernel — a collision.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <h2>2 · Verdict</h2>
    <div id="verdict" class="verdict"> </div>
    <div class="hint" id="detail"></div>
    <div class="hint">
      <b>Logical Invariance Theorem.</b> Over a structureless carrier of any cardinality,
      an interpretation of finitely many coordinates is recoverable from structural truth
      precisely when it depends only on the kernel of the tuple. Two tuples with the same
      kernel are always carried onto one another by some permutation of the carrier, so
      no permutation-invariant relation can separate them; conversely a permutation never
      changes a kernel. Equality survives; order does not, because <code>(0,1)</code> and
      <code>(1,0)</code> have the same kernel and opposite order values. The finiteness of
      the arity is essential: for infinitely many coordinates the classification fails,
      since <code>n ↦ 2n</code> and <code>n ↦ n</code> share a kernel yet only the second
      is surjective.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
"use strict";

let carrier = 3, arity = 2, table = new Map();   // tuple string -> boolean

function tuples(n, k){
  if(k === 0) return [[]];
  const out = [];
  for(const rest of tuples(n, k-1))
    for(let x = 0; x < n; x++) out.push([x, ...rest]);
  return out;
}

function kernelKey(t){
  // canonical form of the equality pattern: first-occurrence renaming
  const map = new Map(); let next = 0;
  return t.map(x => { if(!map.has(x)) map.set(x, next++); return map.get(x); }).join("");
}

function kernelLabel(t){
  const names = "xyz".split("");
  const map = new Map(); let next = 0;
  const pat = t.map(x => { if(!map.has(x)) map.set(x, next++); return map.get(x); });
  // e.g. (0,0,1) -> "x = y ≠ z"
  const parts = [];
  for(let i = 1; i < pat.length; i++)
    parts.push(names[i-1] + (pat[i] === pat[i-1] ? " = " : " ≠ ") + names[i]);
  // also record non-adjacent coincidences for arity 3
  if(pat.length === 3 && pat[0] === pat[2] && pat[0] !== pat[1]) parts.push("x = z");
  if(pat.length === 3 && pat[0] !== pat[2] && pat[0] === pat[1]) parts.push("x ≠ z");
  return parts.join(",  ");
}

function key(t){ return t.join(","); }

function groups(){
  const g = new Map();
  for(const t of tuples(carrier, arity)){
    const k = kernelKey(t);
    if(!g.has(k)) g.set(k, {label: kernelLabel(t), items: []});
    g.get(k).items.push(t);
  }
  return g;
}

function isKernelDetermined(){
  const bad = [];
  for(const [, grp] of groups()){
    const values = grp.items.map(t => !!table.get(key(t)));
    if(values.some(v => v !== values[0])){
      const yes = grp.items.filter(t => table.get(key(t)));
      const no  = grp.items.filter(t => !table.get(key(t)));
      bad.push({label: grp.label, yes, no, items: grp.items});
    }
  }
  return bad;
}

function* permutations(n){
  const a = Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>i), c = new Array(n).fill(0);
  yield a.slice();
  let i = 0;
  while(i < n){
    if(c[i] < i){
      const j = (i % 2 === 0) ? 0 : c[i];
      [a[i],a[j]] = [a[j],a[i]];
      yield a.slice(); c[i]++; i = 0;
    } else { c[i] = 0; i++; }
  }
}

function isPermutationInvariant(){
  for(const s of permutations(carrier))
    for(const t of tuples(carrier, arity))
      if(!!table.get(key(t)) !== !!table.get(key(t.map(x => s[x])))) return {ok:false, perm:s, t};
  return {ok:true};
}

function setPreset(name){
  table = new Map();
  for(const t of tuples(carrier, arity)){
    let v = false;
    switch(name){
      case "eq":      v = t.every(x => x === t[0]); break;
      case "neq":     v = !t.every(x => x === t[0]); break;
      case "lt":      v = t.every((x,i) => i === 0 || t[i-1] < x); break;
      case "first":   v = t[0] === 0; break;
      case "alldist": v = new Set(t).size === t.length; break;
      case "cyc":     v = t.every((x,i) => i === 0 || x === (t[i-1]+1) % carrier); break;
      default:        v = false;
    }
    table.set(key(t), v);
  }
}

function render(){
  const bad = isKernelDetermined();
  const clashing = new Set();
  bad.forEach(b => b.items.forEach(t => clashing.add(key(t))));

  let html = "";
  for(const [, grp] of groups()){
    html += `<div class="kernelbox"><h3>kernel:  ${grp.label || "(single coordinate)"}
              ·  ${grp.items.length} tuples</h3><div class="grid">`;
    for(const t of grp.items){
      const on = !!table.get(key(t));
      const cls = "cell " + (on ? "on" : "off") + (clashing.has(key(t)) ? " clash" : "");
      html += `<div class="${cls}" data-t="${key(t)}">(${t.join(",")})<br>${on ? "true" : "false"}</div>`;
    }
    html += `</div></div>`;
  }
  document.getElementById("classes").innerHTML = html;
  document.querySelectorAll(".cell").forEach(c => {
    c.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const k = c.dataset.t;
      table.set(k, !table.get(k));
      render();
    });
  });

  const inv = isPermutationInvariant();
  const verdict = document.getElementById("verdict");
  const detail = document.getElementById("detail");
  if(bad.length === 0){
    verdict.innerHTML = `<span class="ok">✓ Logical.</span> This relation is constant on
      every kernel class, hence invariant under every permutation of the carrier
      (independently confirmed: ${inv.ok ? "yes" : "no"}). It is therefore recoverable
      from structural truth — it is built from equality alone.`;
    const kinds = [...groups()].filter(([,g]) => table.get(key(g.items[0])))
                               .map(([,g]) => g.label || "—");
    detail.innerHTML = kinds.length
      ? `It holds exactly of the tuples with kernel:  <b>${kinds.join("</b>;  <b>")}</b>.`
      : `It holds of nothing at all — the empty relation, trivially logical.`;
  } else {
    const b = bad[0];
    const y = b.yes[0], nn = b.no[0];
    verdict.innerHTML = `<span class="no">✗ Not logical.</span> The tuples
      (${y.join(",")}) and (${nn.join(",")}) have the <b>same</b> equality pattern
      (${b.label}) but you assigned them different truth values. Some permutation of the
      carrier carries the first onto the second, so this relation collides with itself
      and no structureless set can carry it.`;
    detail.innerHTML = `${bad.length} kernel class${bad.length>1?"es":""} currently
      disagree${bad.length>1?"":"s"} internally. Independent check by brute force over all
      ${factorial(carrier)} permutations: permutation-invariant = <b>${inv.ok}</b>
      — the two tests always agree, which is the content of the theorem.`;
  }
}

function factorial(n){ return n <= 1 ? 1 : n * factorial(n-1); }

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const reload = () => {
    carrier = +document.getElementById("carrier").value;
    arity = +document.getElementById("arity").value;
    setPreset(document.getElementById("preset").value);
    render();
  };
  document.getElementById("carrier").addEventListener("change", reload);
  document.getElementById("arity").addEventListener("change", reload);
  document.getElementById("preset").addEventListener("change", reload);
  document.getElementById("clear").addEventListener("click", () => {
    setPreset("empty"); render();
  });
  document.getElementById("fix").addEventListener("click", () => {
    // Make the relation kernel-determined by majority vote inside each class.
    for(const [, grp] of groups()){
      const yes = grp.items.filter(t => table.get(key(t))).length;
      const v = yes * 2 >= grp.items.length;
      grp.items.forEach(t => table.set(key(t), v));
    }
    render();
  });
  document.getElementById("preset").value = "lt";
  reload();
});
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    }
  ],
  "interactive_layout": "# The Definability Boundary: What a Structure Can and Cannot Mean

*A guided tour, from a labelled triangle to an exact conservation law for meaning.*

---

## 0. A puzzle to start with

Draw an equilateral triangle and label its corners $A$, $B$, $C$. Hand the drawing to
someone allowed to rotate and reflect it freely, and ask: **which corner was $A$?**

They cannot tell you. The labels are not part of the triangle. They are something you
brought from outside, laid over a shape with no opinion about which of its three
identical corners deserves which letter.

That small observation is the seed of everything below. By the end of this page you will
be able to say, for any structure and any labelling, *exactly* how much of the labelling
survives — and you will know the single natural number that measures what is lost.

---

## 1. The setup: structures, symmetries, meanings

Fix a set $M$ — points, vertices of a graph, positions on a board. Its **symmetries**
form a group $G$: the transformations preserving whatever structure $M$ carries.

Two elements $x, y \in M$ are **structurally indistinguishable**, written $x \sim y$, when
some symmetry carries one to the other: $g \cdot x = y$ for some $g \in G$. From the
inside, indistinguishable elements are the same element wearing different disguises.

An **external interpretation** is any function
$$I : M \longrightarrow V$$
assigning to each element a *meaning* from a value set $V$ living outside the structure:
a colour, a name, a price, a truth value.

The whole subject is one question: **which interpretations can the structure itself
remember?**

<details>
<summary>Click for the precise definition of "remember"</summary>

Write $M/G$ for the set of symmetry classes and $\pi : M \to M/G$ for the map sending an
element to its own class. Say $I$ is **recoverable from structural truth** if there is a
function $F : M/G \to V$ with $F(\pi(x)) = I(x)$ for every $x$.

Read this as: the meaning was never really external. It was a function of the structural
data all along, and $F$ is the recipe.

</details>

---

## 2. Play first, theorise later

Before any theorem, get your hands dirty. Pick a structure, paint meanings onto it, and
watch which paintings survive and which collide. Try to find, for each structure, the
finest painting it can hold.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Three things to try:

1. **The path $0-1-2$.** Give the two endpoints different colours. The widget flags a
   collision: the endpoint swap is a symmetry, so the path cannot distinguish them. Now
   colour the endpoints alike and the midpoint differently — that survives, and it is
   exactly the degree function.
2. **The complete graph $K_4$.** Try to find *any* non-constant painting that survives.
   You cannot. Maximal symmetry annihilates all external meaning.
3. **The rigid graph.** Every painting survives. Nothing is lost. Notice the exponent
   $\ell$ in the panel drop to $0$.

---

## 3. The first theorem: descent

What you just discovered by hand is a theorem.

> **Orbit Descent Theorem.** An external interpretation $I : M \to V$ is recoverable from
> structural truth **if and only if** it is *orbit-constant*: $x \sim y \implies I(x) = I(y)$.
> Moreover the recovering function $F$, when it exists, is **unique**.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proof</summary>

($\Rightarrow$) If $F(\pi(x)) = I(x)$ and $x \sim y$, then $\pi(x) = \pi(y)$, so
$I(x) = F(\pi(x)) = F(\pi(y)) = I(y)$.

($\Leftarrow$) If $I$ is orbit-constant it is constant on each fibre of $\pi$, so setting
$F([x]) := I(x)$ is well defined, and by construction $F \circ \pi = I$.

Uniqueness: $\pi$ is surjective, so every class is $[x]$ for some $x$, and any two
recoveries agree there.

</details>

The uniqueness clause has a slicker form. The **orbit map** $\pi$ is itself a recoverable
interpretation, and it is the *finest* one: every recoverable interpretation factors
through it, in exactly one way. So $\pi$ is not merely *an* invariant of $M$ — it is *the*
invariant, and every other structurally-carried meaning is a renaming of it. It follows
at once that recoverable interpretations are closed under post-composition with any
function (renaming meanings never destroys recoverability) and under pairing.

The negative half is the contrapositive, and it deserves its own name.

> **Meaning collision.** If $x \sim y$ but $I(x) \neq I(y)$, then $I$ is not recoverable.
> One disagreement inside one symmetry class destroys the whole interpretation.

Pushed to the extreme: under the *full* symmetric group any two elements are
indistinguishable, so an interpretation survives if and only if it is globally constant.
A bare set of five objects holds no external meaning beyond a single global choice. This
is the same phenomenon that makes it meaningless to ask which of two electrons is "the
first one".

---

## 4. Counting the survivors, and the exponent

Now count. Let $M$ be finite with $n$ elements, $V$ finite, and suppose the symmetries
carve $M$ into $k$ symmetry classes.

There are $|V|^n$ interpretations in total. A recoverable one is exactly a function on
the class space, so there are $|V|^k$ of them. Dividing:

$$|V|^{n} \;=\; \underbrace{|V|^{k}}_{\text{recoverable}} \;\times\; \underbrace{|V|^{\,n-k}}_{\text{pure loss}}.$$

> **Definition.** The **meaning-loss exponent** is $\ell(M) = n - k = |M| - \#\text{classes}$.
> The recoverable interpretations form a family exactly $|V|^{\ell(M)}$ times smaller than
> the family of all interpretations.

Notice what $\ell$ does *not* depend on: the value set. It is an invariant of the
structure alone.

{{visualization:0}}

Read the atlas above: vertices sharing a colour are indistinguishable, and $\ell$ counts
the surplus. A single orbit of size $m$ contributes $m-1$ duplicates; $n$ singleton
orbits contribute nothing.

---

## 5. What the exponent obeys

The exponent turns out to be a well-behaved structural invariant, with three properties
that between them pin it down.

> **Additivity.** $\ell(M \sqcup N) = \ell(M) + \ell(N)$ for the disjoint union of two
> models acted on blockwise.

> **Rigidity criterion.** $\ell(M) = 0$ if and only if $M$ is *rigid* (indistinguishable
> elements are equal) if and only if **every** external interpretation is recoverable.

> **Orbit decomposition.** $\ell(M) = \sum_{\text{classes } O} (|O| - 1)$: the exponent
> counts the duplicate elements inside classes, and nothing else.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proofs</summary>

*Additivity.* The symmetries preserve each summand, so the class space of $M \sqcup N$ is
canonically the disjoint union of the two class spaces; hence classes add, elements add,
and their difference adds. (The blockwise hypothesis matters: the full automorphism group
of a disjoint union of two *isomorphic* graphs also swaps the copies, merging classes and
pushing the exponent above the sum.)

*Rigidity.* $\ell(M) = 0$ says $|M| = |M/G|$. The class map is always surjective, so
equality of finite cardinalities makes it injective, which is rigidity; and conversely.
For the "every interpretation" reading: if the model is rigid, orbit constancy is
vacuous. If it is not, pick $x \sim y$ with $x \neq y$ and two distinct values
$v_0 \neq v_1$; the interpretation sending $x$ to $v_0$ and everything else to $v_1$
collides.

*Decomposition.* The classes partition $M$, so $|M| = \sum_O |O|$; every class is
non-empty, so subtracting one per class is an honest subtraction, and
$\sum_O (|O| - 1) = |M| - k = \ell(M)$.

</details>

Additivity is the signature of an *extensive* quantity, like entropy or dimension rather
than like a probability: independent systems side by side have exactly the sum of their
capacities for forgetting.

Here is the census that checks all of this exhaustively — not on samples, on *every*
graph up to five vertices, and on every pair up to four.

{{demo:1}}

And here is the trade-off in a picture: as the symmetry group grows, the classes coarsen,
the exponent rises, and the stock of recoverable meanings collapses.

{{visualization:1}}

---

## 6. A bridge to classical combinatorics

The count of recoverable interpretations plugs straight into group theory. With
$V = \{\text{true}, \text{false}\}$ there are $R = 2^{k}$ recoverable interpretations, and
the classical orbit-counting lemma computes $k$ as the average number of points a
symmetry leaves fixed. Substituting:

$$2^{\;\sum_{g \in G} |\mathrm{Fix}(g)|} \;=\; R^{\,|G|}.$$

Semantics on the left of the equals sign; fixed-point counts on the right. The number of
meanings a structure can hold *is* a character sum. Read in the classical direction, this
is the statement that counting colourings up to symmetry is counting recoverable
interpretations — the enumeration technique of
[Burnside's lemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside%27s_lemma) in semantic dress.

{{algorithm:3}}

---

## 7. Can we *say* what survives?

Descent tells us which meanings survive. A different question is whether some *language*
picks out exactly the survivors.

Call a family $\mathcal{L}$ of subsets of $M$ an **invariant language** if it contains
$\emptyset$, is closed under complement and union, and — the essential clause — every set
in it is invariant under all symmetries. That last clause is what makes the language a
language *about the structure*, blind to anything the structure cannot see. Say $I$ is
**definable** in $\mathcal{L}$ when each of its meaning-fibres $\{x : I(x) = v\}$ lies in
$\mathcal{L}$.

The first surprise is that a natural-looking conjecture — "recoverable means orbit-constant
*and* definable" — contains a redundancy.

> **Redundancy.** In *any* invariant language, definability already implies orbit
> constancy. So "orbit-constant and definable" says exactly "definable".

<details>
<summary>Click for the one-line proof</summary>

Let $y = g \cdot x$. The fibre $I^{-1}(I(x))$ is definable, hence invariant, and contains
$x$; so it contains $g \cdot x = y$, i.e. $I(y) = I(x)$.

</details>

So definability is the *stronger* notion. How much stronger? Entirely depends on the
language, and the answer splits into three regimes.

### Regime 1: the largest language — perfect agreement

Take $\mathcal{O}$ to be the family of **all** invariant sets. It is an invariant
language, and every invariant language sits inside it.

> **Maximal-Language Theorem.** An interpretation is recoverable from structural truth if
> and only if it is definable in $\mathcal{O}$ — with no finiteness hypothesis whatsoever.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proof</summary>

One direction is the redundancy lemma. For the other, if $I$ is orbit-constant,
$x \in I^{-1}(v)$ and $g \in G$, then $I(g\cdot x) = I(x) = v$, so every fibre is
invariant and therefore belongs to $\mathcal{O}$.

</details>

### Regime 2: bounded languages on infinite carriers — a real gap

Now take $M = \mathbb{N}$ with the **trivial** symmetry group. Indistinguishability is
equality, so *every* interpretation is recoverable. Take the invariant language of sets
that are finite or cofinite — a formula may pin down only finitely much information, or
its negation may. And take parity, $I(n) = [\,n \text{ even}\,]$.

> **The boundary is real.** Parity is recoverable but not definable in the finite/cofinite
> invariant language: its fibre, the even numbers, is infinite with infinite complement.
> On infinite carriers, orbit constancy is strictly weaker than definability.

What fails is not invariance but *expressive capacity*: with the trivial group every
subset of $\mathbb{N}$ is invariant, so parity is definable in the maximal language. It is
the bounded language that cannot reach it.

### Regime 3: finite carriers — total collapse

Enrich the language with **orbit-counting modalities**: one predicate naming each symmetry
class, plus Boolean combinations.

> **Finite Classification.** For an interpretation of a finite structure, the following
> are equivalent: (i) recoverable from structural truth; (ii) constant on symmetry
> classes; (iii) definable in the largest invariant language; (iv) every fibre is a
> Boolean combination of class predicates.

<details>
<summary>Click for the hard clause, and the algorithm hiding inside it</summary>

The content is that on a finite structure *every* invariant set is a Boolean combination
of classes. Proof by strong induction on the size of an invariant set $S$: if $S$ is
empty we are done; otherwise pick $x \in S$, note that invariance forces the whole class
of $x$ inside $S$, and apply the induction hypothesis to the strictly smaller invariant
set $S \setminus [x]$. Then $S = [x] \cup (S \setminus [x])$.

The proof is an algorithm — peel classes off one at a time — and it terminates in at most
$\#\text{classes}$ rounds, returning the *normal form* of any invariant predicate.

</details>

{{algorithm:2}}

And the enrichment is genuinely necessary, not a convenience: in the *trivial* invariant
language (only $\emptyset$ and everything) no non-constant interpretation is definable at
all. So as soon as a finite structure has two distinct classes, adding counting modalities
strictly increases expressive power.

---

## 8. Only equality is logical

Now interpret *tuples* instead of points, over a carrier with **no** structure, so that
every permutation is a symmetry. Define the **kernel** of a tuple to be its pattern of
coincidences: which coordinates equal which.

> **Logical Invariance Theorem.** Over a structureless carrier of *any* cardinality, an
> interpretation of tuples with finitely many coordinates is recoverable from structural
> truth if and only if it depends only on the kernel of the tuple.

This is the exact form of the classical dictum that the only genuinely
[logical notions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_constant) — those invariant under
all permutations of the universe — are the ones built from equality. Build a relation by
hand and see for yourself:

{{interactive_demo:1}}

Try the strict order preset. The widget marks the collision immediately: $(0,1)$ and
$(1,0)$ have identical equality patterns but opposite order values. On a bare set, *order
is not a relation the set can carry*. It is something we bring.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the proof, and the transport lemma that powers it</summary>

*Transport lemma.* If two finitely-indexed tuples $f$ and $g$ have the same kernel, then
$f(i) \mapsto g(i)$ is a well-defined injection on the finite set $\mathrm{ran}(f)$ — well
defined because $f(i) = f(j) \Rightarrow g(i) = g(j)$, injective because the converse
implication also holds. Extend it to a permutation of the whole carrier: if the carrier is
finite, a partial injection of a finite set into itself extends by counting; if it is
infinite, the domain has cardinality strictly below that of the carrier, and such a
partial injection always extends to a bijection.

*Theorem.* If $f$ and $g$ share a kernel, transport gives $\sigma$ with $\sigma \cdot f = g$,
so orbit constancy forces $I(f) = I(g)$. Conversely a permutation never changes a kernel,
since it is a bijection, so a kernel-determined interpretation is orbit-constant.

</details>

The finiteness of the *arity* is essential, and cheaply so:

> **Sharpness.** For infinitely many coordinates the classification fails. Surjectivity of
> a sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is permutation-invariant, hence recoverable; yet
> $n \mapsto 2n$ and $n \mapsto n$ are both injective, so they share a kernel, and only the
> second is surjective.

{{demo:2}}

---

## 9. The structure knows its own symmetries

One last turn, and the most self-referential. Everything so far took the symmetry group as
given. Reverse the arrow: *how much of the group is visible in the meanings it permits?*

All of it — provided interpretations may speak about **configurations**, whole tuples of
elements, rather than single points.

> **Reconstruction Theorem.** A permutation $\sigma$ belongs to the symmetry group $G$ if
> and only if it preserves every $G$-recoverable interpretation of configurations.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the self-referential trick that proves it</summary>

Given $G$, consider the **membership interpretation**: a configuration is declared
meaningful precisely when it *is* an element of $G$, read as a tuple. This is
$G$-recoverable, because $G$ is closed under multiplication and inverses: for
$\sigma \in G$, $f \in G \iff \sigma f \in G$.

Now suppose $\sigma$ preserves everything recoverable. Apply it to the identity
configuration. Since the identity configuration is meaningful (witnessed by $1 \in G$), so
is $\sigma \cdot \mathrm{id}$ — which is the tuple $a \mapsto \sigma(a)$. Hence
$\sigma \in G$.

</details>

The consequences cascade. The map from a symmetry group to its recoverable theory is
**injective**: distinct groups have genuinely distinct stocks of meanings. It is
order-reversing, and *strictly* so — a strictly larger group has a strictly smaller
theory. Together with the reverse construction (a theory to the group preserving it) one
gets a [Galois connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galois_connection) in which
symmetry groups are exactly the closed objects on their side.

The moral for the whole programme: the recoverability boundary is not an artefact of how
we chose to present the group. **Structural truth determines its own symmetries.**

---

## 11. Where this shows up

- **Databases.** A query is meaningful only if invariant under renaming the entities — the
  classical *genericity* requirement. Descent characterises which annotations survive
  renaming; the exponent counts how much a schema with symmetry destroys.
- **Physics.** Gauge-dependent quantities are exactly the non-recoverable interpretations.
  The distinction between the vector potential and the field strength is the distinction
  between a meaning that collides and one that survives.
- **Machine learning.** An [equivariant model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equivariant_map)
  can only represent orbit-constant functions of its input; $\ell$ is a hard,
  architecture-independent bound on what symmetry costs in expressivity, and additivity
  says the bound behaves predictably when independent inputs are concatenated.
- **Philosophy of logic.** The permutation-invariance criterion for logicality, with an
  explicit and provably sharp finiteness hypothesis.
- **Combinatorics and chemistry.** Counting essentially-different colourings of a
  symmetric object *is* counting recoverable interpretations.

---

## 12. Where to go next

A few directions the theory points at, none of them settled here.

- **Presentable languages beyond the finite.** Between the bounded language (too weak) and
  the maximal one (not finitely presented), which invariant languages on infinite carriers
  capture recoverability? For
  [oligomorphic groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligomorphic_group) — finitely many
  orbits on $n$-tuples for each $n$ — a counting language over orbits of tuples should
  suffice, giving an infinite analogue of the finite collapse.
- **A continuous exponent.** For a compact group acting on a manifold, $\ell$ should become
  $\dim M - \dim(M/G)$, the generic orbit dimension. Do additivity, rigidity and orbit
  decomposition survive, and does a measure-theoretic version compute an entropy?
- **Intermediate arities.** The kernel classification holds at finite arity and fails at
  $\aleph_0$; for a carrier of size $\kappa$ one expects it to hold below $\kappa$ and fail
  at $\kappa$, since transport fails exactly when a tuple's range can exhaust the carrier.
- **Products and quotients.** Additivity handles disjoint unions. What is $\ell(M \times N)$
  for the diagonal action, and how does $\ell$ move as the acting group shrinks or grows?

---

## The shape of the answer

Start with a naive guess: meaning survives when it is orbit-constant and definable. What
the theory shows is that this splits into three separate truths. In the maximal invariant
language, recoverability and definability are the *same thing*, with no hypotheses. In
bounded languages on infinite carriers, definability is *strictly stronger*, and parity is
the witness. On finite carriers everything collapses to a single four-way equivalence, and
the counting modalities that make it work are provably necessary.

And underneath all three sits one number,
$$\ell(M) = |M| - \#\text{symmetry classes},$$
additive over disjoint unions, vanishing exactly on rigid structures, and equal to the
count of duplicate elements inside classes — the exact quantity of external meaning that
structure destroys.

# A Galois Correspondence Between Symmetry Groups and Interpretation Theories

The companion files show that an external interpretation `I : M → V` descends to
structural truth exactly when it is constant on the orbits of the symmetry group
`G` (`ExternalInterpretationDefinability.recoverable_iff_orbitConstant`).  That
result takes the group as given.  This file asks the *inverse* question:

> How much of the symmetry group is visible in the collection of interpretations
> it makes recoverable?

The answer is: **all of it**, provided the interpretations are allowed to speak
about *configurations* (tuples of elements) rather than single points.  Writing
`Config α = α → α` for the space of `α`-indexed configurations, with a
permutation acting pointwise on values, we prove

* `mem_iff_preserves_recoverable` — a permutation `σ` lies in `G` **iff** it
  preserves every `G`-recoverable interpretation of configurations.  This is a
  Krasner-style closure theorem for permutation groups: no proper overgroup and
  no proper subgroup can have the same recoverable theory.
* `invTheory_injective` — hence `G ↦ (its recoverable theory)` is injective, so
  the lattice of symmetry groups embeds into the lattice of interpretation
  theories, antitonically (`invTheory_antitone`, `symGroup_antitone`).
* `symGroup_invTheory` / `invTheory_symGroup_invTheory` — the pair
  (`symGroup`, `invTheory`) is a Galois connection whose group-side closure
  operator is the identity: symmetry groups are exactly the Galois-closed
  objects.
* `invTheory_lt_of_lt` — strict inclusions of groups give strict inclusions of
  theories, and `bool_theories_ne` is a concrete two-element witness.

The moral for the definability programme: "structural truth" determines its own
symmetry group, so the recoverability boundary studied in the other files is an
intrinsic invariant of the theory, not an artefact of the chosen group
presentation.

import Mathlib
import Catalog.Applications.ExternalInterpretationDefinability

namespace ExternalInterpretationGalois

open ExternalInterpretationDefinability

universe u

variable {α : Type u}

/-! ## Configurations and the pointwise action -/

/-- The space of **configurations**: `α`-indexed tuples of elements of `α`.
Interpretations of configurations are the natural test objects for how much a
symmetry group is seen by structural truth. -/
def Config (α : Type u) : Type u := α → α

instance : MulAction (Equiv.Perm α) (Config α) where
  smul σ f := fun a => σ (f a)
  one_smul _ := rfl
  mul_smul _ _ _ := rfl

lemma smul_config_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (f : Config α) (a : α) :
    (σ • f) a = σ (f a) := rfl

/-- The identity configuration, i.e. the tuple listing every element of `α` once. -/
def idConfig (α : Type u) : Config α := fun a => a

lemma smul_idConfig (σ : Equiv.Perm α) : σ • idConfig α = (fun a => σ a) := rfl

/-! ## The two sides of the correspondence -/

/-- An **interpretation theory**: a set of propositional interpretations of
configurations. -/
abbrev Theory (α : Type u) : Type u := Set (Config α → Prop)

/-- The theory of a symmetry group: all interpretations recoverable from the
structural truth `G` provides. -/
def invTheory (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) : Theory α :=
  {I | Recoverable G I}

/-- A permutation **preserves** an interpretation when it cannot change any
meaning. -/
def Preserves (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (I : Config α → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Config α, I (σ • f) = I f

/-- The symmetry group of a theory: all permutations preserving every
interpretation in it.  This is a subgroup. -/
def symGroup (S : Theory α) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α) where
  carrier := {σ | ∀ I ∈ S, Preserves σ I}
  one_mem' := by
    intro I _ f
    simp [one_smul]
  mul_mem' := by
    intro σ τ hσ hτ I hI f
    rw [mul_smul, hσ I hI, hτ I hI]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro σ hσ I hI f
    have := hσ I hI (σ⁻¹ • f)
    rw [smul_inv_smul] at this
    exact this.symm

lemma mem_symGroup {S : Theory α} {σ : Equiv.Perm α} :
    σ ∈ symGroup S ↔ ∀ I ∈ S, Preserves σ I := Iff.rfl

/-! ## Recoverable interpretations of configurations -/

/-- Membership in a group's theory, unfolded to orbit constancy. -/
lemma mem_invTheory_iff {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} {I : Config α → Prop} :
    I ∈ invTheory G ↔ ∀ (g : G) (f : Config α), I (g • f) = I f := by
  constructor
  · intro hI g f
    have h := (recoverable_iff_orbitConstant (G := G) I).mp hI (⟨g, rfl⟩ : Indist G f (g • f))
    exact propext ⟨fun hx => h ▸ hx, fun hx => h ▸ hx⟩
  · intro h
    refine (recoverable_iff_orbitConstant (G := G) I).mpr ?_
    rintro x y ⟨g, rfl⟩
    exact (h g x).symm

/-- Every element of `G` preserves every interpretation in `G`'s theory: one half
of the closure theorem, and the easy one. -/
lemma le_symGroup_invTheory (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) :
    G ≤ symGroup (invTheory G) := by
  intro σ hσ I hI f
  exact mem_invTheory_iff.mp hI ⟨σ, hσ⟩ f

/-- The **membership interpretation** of a subgroup: a configuration is
meaningful exactly when it is (the underlying tuple of) a symmetry in `G`.  This
is the interpretation that detects `G` itself. -/
def memInterp (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) : Config α → Prop :=
  fun f => ∃ g : Equiv.Perm α, g ∈ G ∧ (fun a => g a) = f

lemma memInterp_recoverable (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) :
    memInterp G ∈ invTheory G := by
  refine mem_invTheory_iff.mpr ?_
  rintro ⟨σ, hσ⟩ f
  refine propext ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rintro ⟨g, hg, hgf⟩
    refine ⟨σ⁻¹ * g, G.mul_mem (G.inv_mem hσ) hg, ?_⟩
    funext a
    have h1 : g a = σ (f a) := congrArg (fun h => h a) hgf
    simp [Equiv.Perm.coe_mul, h1]
  · rintro ⟨g, hg, hgf⟩
    refine ⟨σ * g, G.mul_mem hσ hg, ?_⟩
    funext a
    have h1 : g a = f a := congrArg (fun h => h a) hgf
    show σ (g a) = σ (f a)
    rw [h1]

/-- **Krasner-style closure theorem.**  A permutation belongs to the symmetry
group exactly when it preserves every interpretation that this group makes
recoverable.  Thus the group is reconstructible from its recoverable theory. -/
theorem mem_iff_preserves_recoverable {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)}
    {σ : Equiv.Perm α} :
    σ ∈ G ↔ ∀ I ∈ invTheory G, Preserves σ I := by
  constructor
  · intro hσ I hI
    exact le_symGroup_invTheory G hσ I hI
  · intro h
    have hpres := h (memInterp G) (memInterp_recoverable G) (idConfig α)
    have hid : memInterp G (idConfig α) := ⟨1, G.one_mem, rfl⟩
    have : memInterp G (σ • idConfig α) := by rw [hpres]; exact hid
    obtain ⟨g, hg, hgf⟩ := this
    have : g = σ := by
      ext a
      have := congrArg (fun h => h a) hgf
      simpa [smul_idConfig] using this
    exact this ▸ hg

/-- **Group-side Galois closure is the identity.** -/
theorem symGroup_invTheory (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) :
    symGroup (invTheory G) = G := by
  ext σ
  exact (mem_iff_preserves_recoverable).symm

/-! ## The Galois connection -/

lemma invTheory_antitone {G H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} (h : G ≤ H) :
    invTheory H ⊆ invTheory G := by
  intro I hI
  refine mem_invTheory_iff.mpr ?_
  rintro ⟨g, hg⟩ f
  exact mem_invTheory_iff.mp hI ⟨g, h hg⟩ f

lemma symGroup_antitone {S T : Theory α} (h : S ⊆ T) : symGroup T ≤ symGroup S :=
  fun _ hσ I hI => hσ I (h hI)

lemma le_symGroup_iff {G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} {S : Theory α} :
    G ≤ symGroup S ↔ S ⊆ invTheory G := by
  constructor
  · intro h I hI
    refine mem_invTheory_iff.mpr ?_
    rintro ⟨g, hg⟩ f
    exact h hg I hI f
  · intro h σ hσ I hI f
    exact mem_invTheory_iff.mp (h hI) ⟨σ, hσ⟩ f

/-- The theory-side closure operator is idempotent on theories of groups. -/
theorem invTheory_symGroup_invTheory (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)) :
    invTheory (symGroup (invTheory G)) = invTheory G := by
  rw [symGroup_invTheory]

/-- **Reconstruction.**  Distinct symmetry groups have distinct recoverable
theories: the map `G ↦ invTheory G` is injective. -/
theorem invTheory_injective :
    Function.Injective (invTheory : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α) → Theory α) := by
  intro G H h
  have := congrArg symGroup h
  rwa [symGroup_invTheory, symGroup_invTheory] at this

/-- A strictly larger symmetry group has a strictly smaller theory: more
symmetry means strictly fewer recoverable meanings. -/
theorem invTheory_lt_of_lt {G H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)} (h : G < H) :
    invTheory H ⊂ invTheory G := by
  refine ⟨invTheory_antitone h.le, ?_⟩
  intro hsub
  have hEq : H = G := invTheory_injective (Set.Subset.antisymm (invTheory_antitone h.le) hsub)
  exact absurd hEq h.ne'

/-! ## A concrete two-element witness -/

/-- On a two-element model the trivial group and the full symmetric group are
distinct, hence – by reconstruction – have genuinely different stocks of
recoverable interpretations. -/
theorem bool_theories_ne :
    invTheory (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Bool)) ≠ invTheory (⊤ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Bool)) := by
  intro h
  have : (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Bool)) = ⊤ := invTheory_injective h
  have hswap : Equiv.swap true false ∈ (⊤ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Bool)) := Subgroup.mem_top _
  rw [← this] at hswap
  have : Equiv.swap true false = (1 : Equiv.Perm Bool) := Subgroup.mem_bot.mp hswap
  have := congrArg (fun e => e true) this
  simp at this

end ExternalInterpretationGalois",

      have hr : (orbitRel G M) a b := hab
      rw [MulAction.orbitRel_apply, MulAction.mem_orbit_iff] at hr
      obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hr

      have hr : (orbitRel G N) a b := hab
      rw [MulAction.orbitRel_apply, MulAction.mem_orbit_iff] at hr
      obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hr
      exact Quotient.sound ⟨g, by rw [← hg]; rfl⟩))

  right_inv := by

theorem card_orbits_sum [Fintype (orbitRel.Quotient G (M ⊕ N))]
    [Fintype (orbitRel.Quotient G M)] [Fintype (orbitRel.Quotient G N)] :
    Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G (M ⊕ N))

  rw [Fintype.card_congr (sumQuotEquiv G M N), Fintype.card_sum]

  have h1 : Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G M) ≤ Fintype.card M := card_orbits_le
  have h2 : Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G N) ≤ Fintype.card N := card_orbits_le
  have hsum := card_orbits_sum (G := G) (M := M) (N := N)
  unfold meaningLoss
  rw [hsum, Fintype.card_sum]

      obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hr

/-! ## Part 0 — Structural indistinguishability -/

/-- Two elements are **structurally indistinguishable** when some automorphism
(element of the acting group `G`) carries one to the other. -/
def Indist (G : Type u) [Group G] [MulAction G M] (x y : M) : Prop := ∃ g : G, g • x = y

lemma indist_refl (x : M) : Indist G x x := ⟨1, one_smul _ _⟩

lemma indist_symm {x y : M} (h : Indist G x y) : Indist G y x := by
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨g⁻¹, by simp⟩

lemma indist_trans {x y z : M} (h₁ : Indist G x y) (h₂ : Indist G y z) : Indist G x z := by
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨h, rfl⟩ := h₂
  exact ⟨h * g, by rw [mul_smul]⟩

/-- Indistinguishability is exactly the Mathlib orbit relation (with arguments
swapped, matching `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`). -/
lemma indist_iff_orbitRel {x y : M} : Indist G x y ↔ (orbitRel G M) y x := by
  rw [MulAction.orbitRel_apply, MulAction.mem_orbit_iff]
  exact Iff.rfl

/-- An interpretation is **orbit-constant** if indistinguishable elements get the
same meaning. -/
def OrbitConstant (G : Type u) [Group G] [MulAction G M] (I : M → V) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x y : M⦄, Indist G x y → I x = I y

/-- An interpretation is **recoverable from structural truth** if it factors
through the quotient of the model by structural indistinguishability. -/
def Recoverable (G : Type u) [Group G] [MulAction G M] (I : M → V) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : orbitRel.Quotient G M → V, ∀ x : M, F (Quotient.mk _ x) = I x

/-! ## Part 1 — Orbit descent -/

/-- **Orbit descent.**  An external interpretation is recoverable from structural
truth precisely when it is constant on automorphism orbits. -/
theorem recoverable_iff_orbitConstant (I : M → V) :
    Recoverable G I ↔ OrbitConstant G I := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨F, hF⟩ x y hxy
    have : (Quotient.mk (orbitRel G M) x) = Quotient.mk _ y :=
      Quotient.sound (indist_iff_orbitRel.mp (indist_symm hxy))
    rw [← hF x, ← hF y, this]
  · intro h
    refine ⟨Quotient.lift I ?_, fun x => rfl⟩
    intro a b hab
    have hr : (orbitRel G M) a b := hab
    rw [MulAction.orbitRel_apply, MulAction.mem_orbit_iff] at hr
    exact (h hr).symm

/-- The structural recovery of an interpretation, when it exists, is unique. -/
theorem recovery_unique {I : M → V} {F₁ F₂ : orbitRel.Quotient G M → V}
    (h₁ : ∀ x : M, F₁ (Quotient.mk _ x) = I x) (h₂ : ∀ x : M, F₂ (Quotient.mk _ x) = I x) :
    F₁ = F₂ := by
  funext q
  induction q using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h x => rw [h₁ x, h₂ x]

/-! ## Part 2 — Meaning collisions: the negative half -/

/-- **Meaning collision.**  If two structurally indistinguishable elements are
assigned different meanings, the interpretation cannot be recovered from
structural truth. -/
theorem not_recoverable_of_collision {I : M → V} {x y : M}
    (hxy : Indist G x y) (hne : I x ≠ I y) : ¬ Recoverable G I := by
  intro h
  exact hne ((recoverable_iff_orbitConstant I).mp h hxy)

/-- Under the *full* symmetric group all elements are indistinguishable, so an
interpretation is recoverable exactly when it is globally constant: maximal
symmetry destroys all external meaning beyond a single value. -/
theorem perm_recoverable_iff_constant (I : M → V) :
    Recoverable (Equiv.Perm M) I ↔ ∀ x y : M, I x = I y := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant]
  constructor
  · intro h x y
    classical
    by_cases hxy : x = y
    · rw [hxy]
    · exact h ⟨Equiv.swap x y, by simp [Equiv.Perm.smul_def, Equiv.swap_apply_left]⟩
  · intro h x y _
    exact h x y

/-- A concrete meaning collision: the identity interpretation on `Bool`, viewed
inside the full symmetry group of `Bool`, is not recoverable. -/
theorem meaning_collision_bool : ¬ Recoverable (Equiv.Perm Bool) (id : Bool → Bool) := by
  intro h
  have := (perm_recoverable_iff_constant (id : Bool → Bool)).mp h true false
  simp at this

/-! ## Part 3 — Invariant languages and definability -/

/-- A set is **invariant** if it is closed under the action of the group. -/
def InvariantSet (G : Type u) [Group G] [MulAction G M] (s : Set M) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : G) ⦃x : M⦄, x ∈ s → g • x ∈ s

/-- An **invariant language** on `M`: a Boolean algebra of subsets of `M`, all of
whose members are invariant under the automorphism group. -/
structure InvLang (G : Type u) (M : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G M] where
  /-- The sets definable by a formula of the language. -/
  Defble : Set M → Prop
  /-- The empty set is definable (by a contradictory formula). -/
  empty_mem : Defble ∅
  /-- Definable sets are closed under negation. -/
  compl_mem : ∀ {s : Set M}, Defble s → Defble sᶜ
  /-- Definable sets are closed under disjunction. -/
  union_mem : ∀ {s t : Set M}, Defble s → Defble t → Defble (s ∪ t)
  /-- Every definable set is invariant: the language sees only structure. -/
  invariant : ∀ {s : Set M}, Defble s → InvariantSet G s

/-- An interpretation is **definable** in an invariant language when each of its
meaning fibres is definable. -/
def Definable (L : InvLang G M) (I : M → V) : Prop := ∀ v : V, L.Defble {x | I x = v}

/-- Definability in an invariant language forces orbit constancy: the necessary
condition of the conjecture holds for every invariant language. -/
theorem definable_orbitConstant {L : InvLang G M} {I : M → V} (h : Definable L I) :
    OrbitConstant G I := by
  intro x y hxy
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := hxy
  have hx : x ∈ {z | I z = I x} := rfl
  have := L.invariant (h (I x)) g hx
  exact this.symm

/-- **The conjunction in the conjecture is redundant.**  "Constant on orbits *and*
definable in the invariant language" says no more than "definable": for an
invariant language the first conjunct is automatic. -/
theorem definable_iff_orbitConstant_and_definable {L : InvLang G M} {I : M → V} :
    Definable L I ↔ (OrbitConstant G I ∧ Definable L I) :=
  ⟨fun h => ⟨definable_orbitConstant h, h⟩, And.right⟩

/-- Definable interpretations are recoverable from structural truth. -/
theorem definable_recoverable {L : InvLang G M} {I : M → V} (h : Definable L I) :
    Recoverable G I :=
  (recoverable_iff_orbitConstant I).mpr (definable_orbitConstant h)

/-! ## Part 4 — Orbit predicates, counting modalities, and finite sufficiency -/

lemma invariantSet_orbit (x : M) : InvariantSet G (orbit G x) := by
  intro g y hy
  exact MulAction.mem_orbit_of_mem_orbit g hy

lemma invariantSet_empty : InvariantSet G (∅ : Set M) := by
  intro g x hx; exact absurd hx (Set.notMem_empty x)

lemma invariantSet_compl {s : Set M} (hs : InvariantSet G s) : InvariantSet G sᶜ := by
  intro g x hx hmem
  exact hx (by simpa using hs g⁻¹ hmem)

lemma invariantSet_union {s t : Set M} (hs : InvariantSet G s) (ht : InvariantSet G t) :
    InvariantSet G (s ∪ t) := by
  rintro g x (hx | hx)
  · exact Or.inl (hs g hx)
  · exact Or.inr (ht g hx)

lemma invariantSet_diff {s t : Set M} (hs : InvariantSet G s) (ht : InvariantSet G t) :
    InvariantSet G (s \ t) := by
  intro g x hx
  refine ⟨hs g hx.1, ?_⟩
  intro hmem
  exact hx.2 (by simpa using ht g⁻¹ hmem)

/-- The **orbit language**: all invariant subsets of `M`.  It is an invariant
language, and by `orbitLang_maximal` the largest one. -/
def orbitLang (G : Type u) (M : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G M] : InvLang G M where
  Defble := InvariantSet G
  empty_mem := invariantSet_empty
  compl_mem := invariantSet_compl
  union_mem := invariantSet_union
  invariant := id

/-- Any invariant language is contained in the orbit language. -/
theorem orbitLang_maximal (L : InvLang G M) {s : Set M} (hs : L.Defble s) :
    (orbitLang G M).Defble s := L.invariant hs

/-- Sets definable by a Boolean combination of **orbit (counting) modalities**:
the smallest Boolean algebra of subsets containing every orbit. -/
inductive CountGen (G : Type u) (M : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G M] : Set M → Prop
  | orbit (x : M) : CountGen G M (MulAction.orbit G x)
  | empty : CountGen G M ∅
  | compl {s : Set M} : CountGen G M s → CountGen G M sᶜ
  | union {s t : Set M} : CountGen G M s → CountGen G M t → CountGen G M (s ∪ t)

lemma CountGen.inter {s t : Set M} (hs : CountGen G M s) (ht : CountGen G M t) :
    CountGen G M (s ∩ t) := by
  have : s ∩ t = (sᶜ ∪ tᶜ)ᶜ := by
    simp [Set.compl_union]
  rw [this]
  exact ((hs.compl.union ht.compl).compl)

lemma CountGen.diff {s t : Set M} (hs : CountGen G M s) (ht : CountGen G M t) :
    CountGen G M (s \ t) := by
  rw [Set.diff_eq]
  exact hs.inter ht.compl

/-- **Soundness of the counting language**: every Boolean combination of orbit
predicates is an invariant set. -/
theorem invariantSet_of_countGen {s : Set M} (h : CountGen G M s) : InvariantSet G s := by
  induction h with
  | orbit x => exact invariantSet_orbit x
  | empty => exact invariantSet_empty
  | compl _ ih => exact invariantSet_compl ih
  | union _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact invariantSet_union ih₁ ih₂

/-- Auxiliary strong induction on the size of an invariant set. -/
private theorem countGen_of_invariantSet_aux [Finite M] :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : Set M), s.ncard = n → InvariantSet G s → CountGen G M s := by
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    intro s hcard hinv
    rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty s with rfl | ⟨x, hx⟩
    · exact CountGen.empty
    · have hsub : orbit G x ⊆ s := by
        rintro y ⟨g, rfl⟩
        exact hinv g hx
      have hxorb : x ∈ orbit G x := MulAction.mem_orbit_self x
      have hss : s \ orbit G x ⊂ s := by
        refine ⟨Set.diff_subset, ?_⟩
        intro hcon
        exact (hcon hx).2 hxorb
      have hfin : s.Finite := Set.toFinite s
      have hlt : (s \ orbit G x).ncard < n := by
        rw [← hcard]; exact Set.ncard_lt_ncard hss hfin
      have hrest : CountGen G M (s \ orbit G x) :=
        ih _ hlt _ rfl (invariantSet_diff hinv (invariantSet_orbit x))
      have hsplit : s = orbit G x ∪ (s \ orbit G x) := by
        rw [Set.union_diff_cancel hsub]
      rw [hsplit]
      exact (CountGen.orbit x).union hrest

/-- **Finite completeness of the counting language.**  On a finite model every
invariant set is a Boolean combination of orbit predicates.  Together with
`invariantSet_of_countGen` this identifies the counting language with the orbit
language. -/
theorem countGen_of_invariantSet [Finite M] {s : Set M} (hs : InvariantSet G s) :
    CountGen G M s := countGen_of_invariantSet_aux s.ncard s rfl hs

/-- On a finite model, the counting language defines exactly the invariant sets. -/
theorem countGen_iff_invariantSet [Finite M] {s : Set M} :
    CountGen G M s ↔ InvariantSet G s :=
  ⟨invariantSet_of_countGen, countGen_of_invariantSet⟩

/-- **The finite collapse.**  On a finite model the three notions coincide:
an external interpretation is recoverable from structural truth iff it is
constant on automorphism orbits iff each of its meaning fibres is a Boolean
combination of orbit-counting predicates. -/
theorem finite_recoverable_iff_definable [Finite M] (I : M → V) :
    Recoverable G I ↔ ∀ v : V, CountGen G M {x | I x = v} := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant]
  constructor
  · intro h v
    refine countGen_of_invariantSet ?_
    intro g x hx
    have : I (g • x) = I x := (h ⟨g, rfl⟩).symm
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢
    rw [this, hx]
  · intro h x y hxy
    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := hxy
    have hx : x ∈ {z | I z = I x} := rfl
    exact (invariantSet_of_countGen (h (I x)) g hx).symm

/-- **The general form of the conjecture.**  Without any finiteness assumption,
recoverability from structural truth is exactly definability in the *maximal*
invariant language, the orbit language.  So the correct general statement is
"recoverable ⟺ definable in the largest invariant language"; the role of the
finite hypothesis is only to replace that language by the concrete Boolean
algebra of orbit-counting predicates. -/
theorem definable_orbitLang_iff_recoverable (I : M → V) :
    Definable (orbitLang G M) I ↔ Recoverable G I := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant]
  refine ⟨definable_orbitConstant, ?_⟩
  intro h v g x hx
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢
  rw [← h ⟨g, rfl⟩, hx]

/-- **Capstone classification.**  On a finite model the four candidate readings
of "the interpretation is fixed by structural truth" agree: recoverability,
orbit constancy, definability in the maximal invariant language, and
definability by Boolean combinations of orbit-counting predicates. -/
theorem classification_finite [Finite M] (I : M → V) :
    [Recoverable G I, OrbitConstant G I, Definable (orbitLang G M) I,
      ∀ v : V, CountGen G M {x | I x = v}].TFAE := by
  tfae_have 1 ↔ 2 := recoverable_iff_orbitConstant I
  tfae_have 1 ↔ 3 := (definable_orbitLang_iff_recoverable I).symm
  tfae_have 1 ↔ 4 := finite_recoverable_iff_definable I
  tfae_finish

/-! ## Part 5 — The infinite boundary: orbit constancy is strictly weaker -/

section InfiniteBoundary

/-- The trivial automorphism group of `ℕ`: the bottom subgroup of `Equiv.Perm ℕ`. -/
abbrev TrivG : Type := (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm ℕ))

lemma trivG_smul (g : TrivG) (n : ℕ) : g • n = n := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := g
  rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hg
  subst hg
  rfl

/-- With a trivial automorphism group, structural indistinguishability is
equality, so *every* interpretation is orbit-constant. -/
theorem trivG_orbitConstant (I : ℕ → V) : OrbitConstant TrivG I := by
  rintro x y ⟨g, rfl⟩
  rw [trivG_smul]

/-- The invariant language of finite-or-cofinite subsets of `ℕ` (the "bounded"
language: a formula may only pin down finitely much information, or its
negation may). -/
def cofiniteLang : InvLang TrivG ℕ where
  Defble s := s.Finite ∨ sᶜ.Finite
  empty_mem := Or.inl Set.finite_empty
  compl_mem := by
    rintro s (h | h)
    · exact Or.inr (by simpa using h)
    · exact Or.inl h
  union_mem := by
    rintro s t (hs | hs) (ht | ht)
    · exact Or.inl (hs.union ht)
    · refine Or.inr (Set.Finite.subset ht ?_)
      intro x hx
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_union, not_or] at hx ⊢
      exact hx.2
    · refine Or.inr (Set.Finite.subset hs ?_)
      intro x hx
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_union, not_or] at hx ⊢
      exact hx.1
    · refine Or.inr (Set.Finite.subset hs ?_)
      intro x hx
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_union, not_or] at hx ⊢
      exact hx.1
  invariant := by
    intro s _ g x hx
    rw [trivG_smul]
    exact hx

/-- The parity interpretation of `ℕ`. -/
def parity : ℕ → Bool := fun n => decide (Even n)

lemma setOf_parity_true : {n : ℕ | parity n = true} = {n | Even n} := by
  ext n; simp [parity]

theorem infinite_evens : {n : ℕ | Even n}.Infinite := by
  refine Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem (f := fun k : ℕ => 2 * k) ?_ ?_
  · intro a b hab
    have h : 2 * a = 2 * b := hab
    omega
  · intro k; exact ⟨k, by ring⟩

theorem infinite_odds : {n : ℕ | Even n}ᶜ.Infinite := by
  refine Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem (f := fun k : ℕ => 2 * k + 1) ?_ ?_
  · intro a b hab
    have h : 2 * a + 1 = 2 * b + 1 := hab
    omega
  · intro k
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Nat.not_even_iff_odd]
    exact ⟨k, rfl⟩

/-- **The boundary is real.**  Parity is orbit-constant (trivially so, the
automorphism group being trivial) yet it is *not* definable in the bounded
invariant language: on infinite models orbit constancy is strictly weaker than
definability, so the definability clause of the conjecture cannot be dropped. -/
theorem parity_not_definable : OrbitConstant TrivG parity ∧ ¬ Definable cofiniteLang parity := by
  refine ⟨trivG_orbitConstant parity, ?_⟩
  intro h
  have hdef := h true
  rw [setOf_parity_true] at hdef
  rcases hdef with hfin | hfin
  · exact infinite_evens hfin
  · exact infinite_odds hfin

/-- Consequently, on infinite models recoverability does *not* imply definability:
there is a recoverable but undefinable interpretation. -/
theorem recoverable_not_definable :
    ∃ I : ℕ → Bool, Recoverable TrivG I ∧ ¬ Definable cofiniteLang I :=
  ⟨parity, (recoverable_iff_orbitConstant parity).mpr (trivG_orbitConstant parity),
    parity_not_definable.2⟩

end InfiniteBoundary

/-! ## Part 6 — Counting the recoverable interpretations (Burnside bridge) -/

/-- Recoverable interpretations correspond bijectively to functions on the orbit
space. -/
def recoverableEquiv (G : Type u) (M : Type v) (V : Type w) [Group G] [MulAction G M] :
    {I : M → V // OrbitConstant G I} ≃ (orbitRel.Quotient G M → V) where
  toFun I := Quotient.lift I.1 (by
    intro a b hab
    have hr : (orbitRel G M) a b := hab
    rw [MulAction.orbitRel_apply, MulAction.mem_orbit_iff] at hr
    exact (I.2 hr).symm)
  invFun F := ⟨fun x => F (Quotient.mk _ x), by
    intro x y hxy
    have : (Quotient.mk (orbitRel G M) x) = Quotient.mk _ y :=
      Quotient.sound (indist_iff_orbitRel.mp (indist_symm hxy))
    simp only
    rw [this]⟩
  left_inv := by rintro ⟨I, hI⟩; rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro F
    funext q
    induction q using Quotient.inductionOn with
    | h x => rfl

/-- **Counting recoverable interpretations.**  There are exactly
`|V| ^ (number of orbits)` interpretations recoverable from structural truth. -/
theorem card_orbitConstant_eq_pow [Fintype M] [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq (orbitRel.Quotient G M)] [Fintype (orbitRel.Quotient G M)]
    [Fintype {I : M → V // OrbitConstant G I}] :
    Fintype.card {I : M → V // OrbitConstant G I}
      = Fintype.card V ^ Fintype.card (orbitRel.Quotient G M) := by
  rw [Fintype.card_congr (recoverableEquiv G M V), Fintype.card_fun]

/-- **Burnside bridge.**  Combining the count of recoverable Boolean
interpretations with the orbit-counting lemma gives a purely group-theoretic
formula: the number of recoverable interpretations, raised to the order of the
automorphism group, equals `2` to the total number of fixed points. -/
theorem burnside_recoverable_count [Fintype G] [Fintype M]
    [DecidableEq (orbitRel.Quotient G M)] [Fintype (orbitRel.Quotient G M)]
    [∀ g : G, Fintype (fixedBy M g)]
    [Fintype {I : M → Bool // OrbitConstant G I}] :
    2 ^ (∑ g : G, Fintype.card (fixedBy M g))
      = (Fintype.card {I : M → Bool // OrbitConstant G I}) ^ Fintype.card G := by
  rw [MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group G M, pow_mul,
    card_orbitConstant_eq_pow (G := G) (M := M) (V := Bool)]

import Catalog.Applications.ExternalInterpretationDefinability

variable {G : Type u} {M : Type v} {V : Type w} [Group G] [MulAction G M]

/-! ## Part A — The orbit map is the universal recoverable interpretation -/

/-- The orbit map, sending an element to its structural equivalence class. -/
def orbitMap (G : Type u) (M : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G M] :
    M → orbitRel.Quotient G M := fun x => Quotient.mk _ x

/-- The orbit map is itself recoverable from structural truth. -/
theorem recoverable_orbitMap : Recoverable G (orbitMap G M) := ⟨id, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- **Universal property.**  Every recoverable interpretation factors through the
orbit map, and does so in exactly one way. -/
theorem recoverable_factors_uniquely {I : M → V} (h : Recoverable G I) :
    ∃! F : orbitRel.Quotient G M → V, ∀ x : M, F (orbitMap G M x) = I x := by
  obtain ⟨F, hF⟩ := h
  refine ⟨F, hF, ?_⟩
  intro F' hF'
  exact recovery_unique hF' hF

/-- Recoverable interpretations are closed under post-composition: renaming the
external meanings never destroys recoverability. -/
theorem Recoverable.comp {W : Type*} {I : M → V} (φ : V → W) (h : Recoverable G I) :
    Recoverable G (fun x => φ (I x)) := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant] at h ⊢
  intro x y hxy
  show φ (I x) = φ (I y)
  rw [h hxy]

/-- Recoverable interpretations are closed under pairing. -/
theorem Recoverable.pair {W : Type*} {I : M → V} {J : M → W}
    (hI : Recoverable G I) (hJ : Recoverable G J) :
    Recoverable G (fun x => (I x, J x)) := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant] at hI hJ ⊢
  intro x y hxy
  show (I x, J x) = (I y, J y)
  rw [hI hxy, hJ hxy]

/-- Conversely, anything obtained from the orbit map by post-composition is
recoverable: the orbit map generates all recoverable interpretations. -/
theorem recoverable_of_factors (φ : orbitRel.Quotient G M → V) :
    Recoverable G (fun x => φ (orbitMap G M x)) :=
  Recoverable.comp φ recoverable_orbitMap

/-! ## Part B — The expressivity gap: counting modalities are necessary -/

/-- The **trivial invariant language**: only the contradictory and the tautologous
formula.  It is invariant, but blind. -/
def trivialLang (G : Type u) (M : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G M] : InvLang G M where
  Defble s := s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ
  empty_mem := Or.inl rfl
  compl_mem := by
    rintro s (rfl | rfl)
    · exact Or.inr (by simp)
    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
  union_mem := by
    rintro s t (rfl | rfl) (rfl | rfl) <;> simp
  invariant := by
    rintro s (rfl | rfl) g x hx
    · exact absurd hx (Set.notMem_empty x)
    · trivial

/-- In the trivial language no non-constant interpretation is definable. -/
theorem not_definable_trivialLang_of_nonconstant {I : M → V} {x y : M} (hne : I x ≠ I y) :
    ¬ Definable (trivialLang G M) I := by

    rw [hemp] at this
    exact this
  · have : y ∈ ({z | I z = I x} : Set M) := by rw [huniv]; trivial
    exact hne this.symm

/-- The indicator interpretation of the orbit of `x`. -/
noncomputable def orbitIndicator (G : Type u) [Group G] [MulAction G M] (x : M) : M → Bool :=
  fun z => if z ∈ orbit G x then true else false

lemma orbitIndicator_self (x : M) : orbitIndicator G x x = true := by
  classical
  simp [orbitIndicator, MulAction.mem_orbit_self]

lemma orbitIndicator_eq_false {x y : M} (h : ¬ Indist G x y) : orbitIndicator G x y = false := by
  classical
  have : y ∉ orbit G x := by
    intro hy
    exact h (MulAction.mem_orbit_iff.mp hy)

  by_cases hmem : z ∈ orbit G x
  · have hg : g • z ∈ orbit G x := MulAction.mem_orbit_of_mem_orbit g hmem

  · have hg : g • z ∉ orbit G x := by
      intro hcon
      exact hmem (by simpa using MulAction.mem_orbit_of_mem_orbit g⁻¹ hcon)
    simp [orbitIndicator, hmem, hg]

  refine countGen_of_invariantSet ?_
  intro g z hz
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hz ⊢
  rw [orbitIndicator_smul]
  exact hz

is definable by a Boolean combination of orbit-counting predicates but is not
definable in the trivial invariant language.  So the finite half of the
conjecture genuinely needs the enrichment of the language. -/
theorem counting_strictly_stronger [Finite M] {x y : M} (hxy : ¬ Indist G x y) :

  · exact (finite_recoverable_iff_definable _).mpr (countGen_orbitIndicator_fibre x)
  · refine not_definable_trivialLang_of_nonconstant (x := x) (y := y) ?_
    rw [orbitIndicator_self, orbitIndicator_eq_false hxy]
    simp

section Graphs

variable {W : Type*}

/-- The automorphism group of a simple graph, as a subgroup of the symmetric
group of its vertex set. -/
def autGroup (Γ : SimpleGraph W) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm W) where
  carrier := {σ | ∀ a b, Γ.Adj (σ a) (σ b) ↔ Γ.Adj a b}
  one_mem' := by intro a b; simp
  mul_mem' := by
    intro σ τ hσ hτ a b
    simp only [Equiv.Perm.coe_mul, Function.comp_apply]
    rw [hσ, hτ]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro σ hσ a b
    rw [← hσ (σ⁻¹ a) (σ⁻¹ b)]
    simp

lemma autGroup_adj {Γ : SimpleGraph W} (σ : autGroup Γ) (a b : W) :
    Γ.Adj (σ • a) (σ • b) ↔ Γ.Adj a b := σ.2 a b

/-- An automorphism permutes neighbourhoods. -/
lemma neighborFinset_smul {Γ : SimpleGraph W} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [DecidableRel Γ.Adj]

    Γ.neighborFinset (σ • v) = (Γ.neighborFinset v).image (fun u => σ • u) := by
  ext z
  simp only [Finset.mem_image, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨(σ : Equiv.Perm W).symm z, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have h2 := σ.2 v ((σ : Equiv.Perm W).symm z)
      simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at h2
      exact h2.mp h
    · show (σ : Equiv.Perm W) ((σ : Equiv.Perm W).symm z) = z
      simp
  · rintro ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
    exact (σ.2 v u).mpr hu

theorem degree_smul {Γ : SimpleGraph W} [Fintype W] [DecidableRel Γ.Adj]
    (σ : autGroup Γ) (v : W) : Γ.degree (σ • v) = Γ.degree v := by
  classical
  rw [SimpleGraph.degree, SimpleGraph.degree, neighborFinset_smul σ v,
    Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (MulAction.injective σ)]

interpretation of a finite graph factors through the automorphism orbit space. -/
theorem degree_recoverable (Γ : SimpleGraph W) [Fintype W] [DecidableRel Γ.Adj] :
    Recoverable (autGroup Γ) (fun v => Γ.degree v) := by
  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant]
  rintro x y ⟨g, rfl⟩
  exact (degree_smul g x).symm

lemma mem_autGroup_completeGraph (σ : Equiv.Perm W) : σ ∈ autGroup (completeGraph W) := by
  intro a b
  show σ a ≠ σ b ↔ a ≠ b
  simp

interpretation is recoverable from structural truth exactly when it is constant:
the graph structure distinguishes no vertex from any other. -/
theorem completeGraph_recoverable_iff_constant {V' : Type*} [DecidableEq W] (I : W → V') :

  rw [recoverable_iff_orbitConstant]

  · intro h x y
    by_cases hxy : x = y
    · rw [hxy]
    · refine h ⟨⟨Equiv.swap x y, mem_autGroup_completeGraph _⟩, ?_⟩
      show Equiv.swap x y x = y
      simp
  · intro h x y _
